MN: Eyes on Manchester – the City and United duo Milan want to bring back to Italy

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan are looking for opportunities to bolster the squad ahead of next season, with a particular eye on the north of England.
  • According to MilanNews, Milan are eyeing Manchester for the January transfer window, but also for next summer.
  • In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan are looking for opportunities to bolster the squad ahead of next season, with a particular eye on the north of England.

According to MilanNews, Milan are eyeing Manchester for the January transfer window, but also for next summer. The directors are presently in a phase of monitoring certain situations that could develop later, to their benefit.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri are also interested in players whose contracts are expiring within the next 18 months, as was the case with Mario Gila this summer, who signed for the Diavolo one year before his contract with Lazio expires.

Sources indicate that bruno Fernandes is one to watch for the upcoming summer transfer window, with his contract expiring in June 2027 but with an option to extend. United’s attempts to extend his deal have so far been unsuccessful, likely due to the player’s desire to try something else.

Fernandes has played at an incredible level in the Premier League in recent years, winning Player of the Year for 2025-26. So far, he has made 341 official appearances for the Red Devils, scoring 113 goals and providing 111 assists.

He’s a key player for the Portuguese national team and he would provide leadership that the squad could lose if players like Luka Modric leave. Moreover, his past in Italy – where he had spells at Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria – could help him integrate more rapidly and effectively.

Fernandes also shares the same agency as Ruben Amorim. The relationship between the two is excellent, and already this summer the Rossoneri had inquired about a possible move for the former Sporting star.

At the other Manchester club, however, there’s an old acquaintance of Italian football who could come back into fashion as early as January: Mateo Kovacic. His contract also expires at the end of the campaign, and he could come in to add depth too.

Given the increasingly certain departure of youngster Christian Comotto, an experienced player like Kovacic – at the right price, in terms of wages – could be useful for Amorim. His situation is being watched, but there will be competition from other clubs, likely in Italy too.

Industry News: Key midfielder set for assessment as latest Blackburn Rovers injury patch emerges for Watford test

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (552 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that blackburn Rovers’ key midfielder Sam Morsy was absent from their 2-2 draw with Burnley after sustaining a knock in training.
  • The experienced Egyptian has been an ever-present in Rovers’ side this term since signing in the summer.
  • It has been revealed that meanwhile, Tom Atcheson is under concussion protocols after coming off early against Burnley, following a hit to the head.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that blackburn Rovers’ key midfielder Sam Morsy was absent from their 2-2 draw with Burnley after sustaining a knock in training. However, he is aiming to return to Championship action on Wednesday night against a managerless Watford.

The experienced Egyptian has been an ever-present in Rovers’ side this term since signing in the summer. Morsy has featured on 14 occasions in the league, but is facing a race to be fit in time. On his fitness, caretaker boss Damien Johnson told the Lancashire Telegraph: “Sam was touch and go for the weekend and is similar. He is still being assessed this morning. We will have more news on that after training.”.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, Tom Atcheson is under concussion protocols after coming off early against Burnley, following a hit to the head. The academy graduate has also been a regular feature with his impressive performances at the heart of defence seeing him keep his place in the Northern Ireland national team.

Recent findings suggest that blackburn Rovers have been spearheaded by the sensational form of Andri Gudjohnsen, who is only behind Will Lankshear in the goalscoring charts with 11 to his name. But, it has been a collective effort to see them sit in 13th place.

Rovers were showing signs of real promise prior to Tony Mowbray stepping away from the dugout, most notably an impressive 2-1 victory over West Ham before the international break, with Morsy and Atcheson firmly part of that.

Morsy has filled the role as the anchor of Rovers’ midfield admirably and has shown his worth as one of the Championship’s finest midfield operators at 35.

Atcheson meanwhile is at the opposite end of his career, but has been just as influential. He usually plays on the right-hand side of the back three and impresses with his desire to orchestrate attacks from deep.

Both Morsy and Atcheson are vital cogs in Blackburn’s machine and they will be desperate to have the pair available for a favourable-looking encounter against a troubled Watford side.

Hoping to close the gap to the play-off places to just two points with a victory, Blackburn will certainly fancy their chances with the opponents registering a solitary victory in their last five outings.

Morsy’s experience has been vital for midfield partner Kristi Montgomery who is enjoying his breakout campaign at Ewood Park, and his quality on the ball is still there for all to see at 36.

Nonetheless, Moussa Baradji stepped up to fill his shoes last time out, while Gady Beyuku also strengthened his case for a starting berth in place of Atcheson so Johnson has a wealth of options should either of his key players be unavailable.

West Ham & Middlesbrough sent warning over what Wolves are doing right now

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (638 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham and Middlesbrough have been warned that Wolves have the potential to win the Championship if they ‘click into gear’.
  • It has been a positive start to life at Molineux for Cesar Peixoto, with his side sitting third and just one point away from league leaders Boro going into the midweek set of fixtures, where Wanderers host lowly Derby.
  • Yet, despite the good position, Wolves fans haven’t been totally convinced by Peixoto or the team, with chants directed against the manager as recently as last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham and Middlesbrough have been warned that Wolves have the potential to win the Championship if they ‘click into gear’.

It has been a positive start to life at Molineux for Cesar Peixoto, with his side sitting third and just one point away from league leaders Boro going into the midweek set of fixtures, where Wanderers host lowly Derby.

Yet, despite the good position, Wolves fans haven’t been totally convinced by Peixoto or the team, with chants directed against the manager as recently as last month.

Even if Wolves haven’t always impressed with their performances, they have found a way of getting results, and they head into the Derby game unbeaten in seven, picking up 17 points in that period.

The latest victory was a 2-1 success over Charlton, which was much more comfortable than the scoreline suggests, as Peixoto’s side were rarely troubled all afternoon.

So, they are building momentum, and speaking on The Pyramid Podcast, Jimmy from the Blades Ramble explained how Wolves have gone under the radar somewhat, as he stated they could still have more to offer, which makes them a huge threat in the title race.

Industry observers note that “Wolves are just getting it done. Even when they haven’t been turning up (performances), they’ve been doing enough. So, it worries me that if they turn it on, and click into gear, and reach another level, they could be the ones.

“This is the opportunity for Wolves though, because everyone remarked West Ham, but Wolves aren’t that far behind West Ham (in terms of quality), but they’ve been overlooked because of West Ham being in the league. It shouldn’t surprise anyone if Wolves go on and win this league (even if) I still think Middlesbrough are the team to beat.”.

There’s no denying that Wolves haven’t been a free-flowing, exciting team to watch for large parts this season, but it should be noted that they are very solid defensively, which gives you a good foundation to pick up points.

Peixoto walked into a club in a very difficult situation, as the fans are understandably furious with the owners for their rapid decline in recent years, and that anger is still there.

Plus, there is a feeling that more promises were broken in the summer because of the way the window played out, which has made it difficult for the supporters to fully embrace Peixoto and the team.

But, to his credit, Peixoto has navigated through that very well in terms of results, and if Wolves can beat Derby, they will be on two points a game after 17, which is a brilliant return.

Many would agree that there should still be more to come from this Wolves side, as whilst they are good defensively, the attacking players haven’t hit the heights many expected.

It has been revealed that mateus Mane and Rodrigo Gomes aren’t showing their best levels consistently, whilst Adam Armstrong is only just scoring regularly after a slow start. Meanwhile, Fer Lopez’s influence on the team has reduced, even if he remains a superb talent, and Jordan James hasn’t really got going in Old Gold.

When you add in that Raul Jimenez has missed most of the season through injury and won’t return until January, it just highlights why people think Wolves are capable of doing so much more.

In a recent development, will Wolves win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

And, that should worry their promotion rivals, because if those attacking players do find their best form, Wolves, on paper, have a team that is capable of putting winning runs together.

So, the challenge for Peixoto and the players is to make that happen, as Wolves do have the talent and squad depth to go all the way this season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s prepares.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

In a recent development, in short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

“Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche stated upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”.

The club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”.

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

In a recent development, krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

Industry News: Freyr Alexandersson emerges as contender for Swansea City job in surprise twist

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Swansea City's hunt for an heir to Vitor Matos has now taken another twist, with the Welsh outfit having set their sights on former Iceland women's head coach Freyr Alexandersson.
  • Swansea were rocked by the news of the departure of former head coach Vitor Matos last week, with the former Liverpool and RB Salzburg coach choosing to head to France and link up with Chelsea-affiliated BlueCo outfit Strasbourg.
  • As a result, a coaching team consisting of Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, and Joe Allen have taken charge of things in Swansea for now as the hunt for Matos' replacement continues, as a surprise new contender has emerged.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swansea City's hunt for an heir to Vitor Matos has now taken another twist, with the Welsh outfit having set their sights on former Iceland women's head coach Freyr Alexandersson.

Swansea were rocked by the news of the departure of former head coach Vitor Matos last week, with the former Liverpool and RB Salzburg coach choosing to head to France and link up with Chelsea-affiliated BlueCo outfit Strasbourg.

As a result, a coaching team consisting of Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, and Joe Allen have taken charge of things in Swansea for now as the hunt for Matos' replacement continues, as a surprise new contender has emerged.

According to The Telegraph's Mike McGrath, Icelandic coach Freyr Alexandersson has emerged as the leading contender for the vacant role at the Swansea.com Stadium, having held talks with the club.

Alexandersson, 44, began his coaching career aged just 26, assisting Valur's women's team in his native Iceland, before spells with Leiknir Reykjavík, Iceland women's national team, Iceland men's national team, Al-Arabi, Lyngby, Kortrijk, SK Brann, and now Rosenborg followed.

Swansea have a partnership with Jamestown Analytics, the same model that Brighton and Hove Albion use to recruit players and staff, and that system has likely played a part in the sounding out of Alexandersson.

The current Rosenborg boss has his side sitting in 4th in the Norwegian Eliteserien as things stand, some 18 points behind league leader Bodo/Glimt, as Swansea are trusting their data with this potential appointment.

Unsurprisingly, Swansea were not entirely pleased with the swift departure of Matos, as with Strasbourg's interest emerging, a deal that saw the former Jürgen Klopp understudy head to France was done barely 48 hours later.

Swansea have received a compensation fee in excess of £5 million for Matos, though having been allowed to build the team in his image and get them flying towards the top of the league, it's not the end of the relationship either party surely would've hoped for.

In a statement released by Swansea, the club barely touched on Matos' exit, saying: "Per RC Strasbourg's announcement, Swansea City acknowledges that Vitor Matos and his coaching staff have left the club.".

Now, the hunt for a replacement continues, with Alexandersson emerging from nowhere to go into pole position for the role, as the Welsh outfit looks to maintain their push for promotion in a fresh era.

What do you make of this potential appointment? Who would you like to see replace Vitor Matos at Swansea? Share your thoughts below!

With Williams and a bunch of Swansea favourites over the years taking the helm for now, the club will hope they can remain in contention for automatic promotion moving forward after this jarring and unexpected period.

Whether Alexandersson will be the correct person to take the club forward remains to be seen, as Swansea are putting their faith in Jamestown Analytics and leaning into the data model fully for this potential appointment.

Time will tell how this one plays out, as Swansea fans won't care who is in charge as long as they can maintain their push towards the top of the Championship and forget all about Matos in due course.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ronnie Edwards was signed permanently from Southampton by Queens Park Rangers and has had particular praise from former QPR and Saints striker Charlie Austin.
  • Having played as both a defensive midfielder and a centre-back since his initial arrival on loan to Queens Park Rangers from Southampton, Edwards has since made one of the two central defensive positions his own this season.
  • Jimmy Dunne has also been excellent as his partner for the majority of games, but Jake Clarke-Salter is also a strong performer at Championship level when fit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ronnie Edwards was signed permanently from Southampton by Queens Park Rangers and has had particular praise from former QPR and Saints striker Charlie Austin.

Having played as both a defensive midfielder and a centre-back since his initial arrival on loan to Queens Park Rangers from Southampton, Edwards has since made one of the two central defensive positions his own this season.

Jimmy Dunne has also been excellent as his partner for the majority of games, but Jake Clarke-Salter is also a strong performer at Championship level when fit. Between them, they are an excellent combination of options for Julien Stephan.

It has been revealed that speaking via his show on The Charlie Austin Football Channel on YouTube, Austin talked up the 23-year-old and noted: "Well, Ronnie Edwards at £4.5 million, come from Southampton. I mean, what a steal that is from Southampton.

Recent findings suggest that "Look, I played against him, Peter. I want to say, when I was at West Brom against Peterborough [United]. And I played against him, I thought, 'This young man, he's tidy. He's good him'. Then I played against QPR I think it was again.

Sources indicate that "I always thought he would go on to bigger things other than Southampton, if I'm being honest without being rude. Or he would use that as a stepping stone and move on but he's gone to QPR.

"He went to QPR on loan, he had a great time there. I mean, listen, I don't think you change a winning team, but listen, I've had my frustrations with Julien at times because he hasn't kept certain players in the team when they performed the game previously.

Sources indicate that "Like with [Rumarn] Burrell, we scored two won one game midweek and then he was dropped at the weekend. I couldn't get my head around it if I'm honest as a centre-forward.".

Edwards emerged at Peterborough, making his senior breakthrough as a teenager before establishing himself as one of League One's most exciting young centre-backs.

His performances earned him a £3 million move to Southampton in 2024 (BBC Sport), having also helped England win the European Under-19 Championship. Edwards is an assured operator in possession, comfortable carrying the ball forward, and breaking lines.

In a recent development, he can find teammates between the lines by punching passes into forward areas, too. He is also proactive in defensive duels, although his aerial ability and tendency to be over-aggressive remain areas for improvement if he is to become a Premier League player.

Now one of the Championship's outstanding defenders at QPR, Southampton may regret selling him for a reported £4.5 million initially (Daily Echo). Had they been a bit more patient, he could be their asset worth a lot more than he is now.

Austin is spot on with his praise of Edwards, who looks increasingly like the sort of defender Southampton should have been building their future around. Allowing a young, homegrown, English talent to slip through their fingers to QPR for so little will be particularly frustrating.

Southampton are understandably focused on securing promotion, and their recruitment reflects that, but sustainable clubs cannot afford to neglect player development, even in the midst of that.

Are you happy with the recent strategy at Southampton? Comment below!

It is something Saints have historically excelled at, producing the likes of Gareth Bale, Theo Walcott, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke Shaw, and James Ward-Prowse, be that in the Premier League, the Championship, or in League One.

It has been revealed that they should pride themselves on that identity and lean into it even more. Developing valuable first-team players is not just tradition for them when it is an key part of building a sustainable football club long-term as well.

Michael Skubala to Lincoln City prediction made as Bristol City pressure mounts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An intriguing prediction has been made on the immediate future of Michael Skubala as the 44-year-old's disappointing start to life as Bristol City head coach continued on Saturday.
  • The Robins were thrashed 5-0 by in-form Norwich City at Ashton Gate on November 7th, before suffering a 2-0 loss to Championship leaders, Middlesbrough.
  • Skubala was handed a three-year contract in the West Country in May after becoming the long-term successor to Roy Hodgson, who was drafted in as head coach in March following Gerhard Struber's somewhat controversial exit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An intriguing prediction has been made on the immediate future of Michael Skubala as the 44-year-old's disappointing start to life as Bristol City head coach continued on Saturday.

The Robins were thrashed 5-0 by in-form Norwich City at Ashton Gate on November 7th, before suffering a 2-0 loss to Championship leaders, Middlesbrough.

Skubala was handed a three-year contract in the West Country in May after becoming the long-term successor to Roy Hodgson, who was drafted in as head coach in March following Gerhard Struber's somewhat controversial exit.

City have won just two of their last 11 Championship matches and have slumped to 18th in the table as a result, accumulating just 18 points.

With his side losing four of the last six games and conceding 12 times during that timeframe, supporters have begun to make their feelings known when it comes to Skubala's tactics.

However, circumstances at his former club, Lincoln City, don't appear to be particularly rosey despite the fact the Imps are residing outside the bottom three, which has caused an interesting debate between EFL pundits, Callum Fowler and Jimmy Smith on the Pyramid podcast.

Skubala has won just five of his first 17 matches in charge of Bristol City, culminating in a win ratio of just 29%, and his future is very much up for debate.

It was recently claimed by Alan Nixon that Ashton Gate chiefs have the money to end his three-year reign prematurely, and that background checks were being made on potential successors.

That is despite the fact Skubala believes he has retained the hierarchy's support, with CEO, Charlie Boss, revealing that a meeting had been held and that the head coach had been afforded the opportunity to turn the tide.

The length of said opportunity remains unclear, but it has got off to the worst possible start despite the lofty position of Saturday's opponents, who netted through Adilson Malanda and David Strelec.

Skubala, of course, masterminded Lincoln's first return to the Championship since the 1960s last season as the Imps won League One at a 12-point canter, amassing 103 points and embarking on a 29-match unbeaten run.

Upon his departure to the Robins, Skubala issued a heartfelt message to supporters after 140 matches in charge, of which 71 ended in victory, but given Lincoln's four-game losing streak under joint-managers Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw, Fowler and Smith discussed the potential for the former head coach to return to the ProAmpac Stadium.

"I stated it lots of times last season about Lincoln, it (Skubala's style) is disgusting," Fowler stated. "It's 'prison football', but in League One, that's class, and when you're someone like Lincoln, I guess that's class.

"For Bristol City who are a 'steady away' side anyway, with the money they've spent, you expect a bit more.".

According to recent reports, when asked if Skubala could return to his former club, Fowler debated: "Would they want him?," to which Smith responded: "Yes. I think when a manager's won the league at a canter, you've got fond memories of him, haven't you.

"We look at Parkinson at Wrexham, and we think, 'what are they doing' if they want to kick on, but there's that connection.".

"Would the players buy into it if he went back," stated Fowler. "I definitely think it could happen, but I don't know if Lincoln are thinking about a sacking at the minute.".

Both then agreed that Skubala may lose his current role by the end of the three-game week.

We have already seen four managers sacked in this season's Championship, with three of the sides opting for a change in the dugout currently below Bristol City in the table, in the form of Burnley, Watford and Preston North End.

Skubala will have no doubt been grateful to have received the backing from the board during the international break, but defeat to Wrexham on Tuesday night would leave them even further adrift from where many expected the Robins to be under his guidance, which is to compete for a second play-off berth in three seasons.

Do you agree with this prediction on Michael Skubala's future? Comment below!

The Red Dragons had endured a slow start to the campaign themselves, but Parkinson's side have accumulated seven points from the last nine available, four of which came in encounters against Middlesbrough and Wolves, making City's task of achieving a vital win all the more difficult.

Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.
  • In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

According to recent reports, around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

Recent findings suggest that extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office remarked in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The Istanbul Governor's Office remarked 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive.

Recent findings suggest that reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

It has been revealed that gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an update.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he stated. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen mentioned: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'.

According to recent reports, galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'.

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray.

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

According to recent reports, villa defender Ian Maatsen noted: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’.

It has been revealed that galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’.

It has been revealed that villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

According to recent reports, repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom).

Will Garnacho’s chance ever come?

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

When the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

Sources indicate that what next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

According to recent reports, born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

In a recent development, yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

According to recent reports, to invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

There were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet quickly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea.

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

Dave Challinor reveals how Barry Bannan can spend even longer at Sheffield Wednesday

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (939 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sheffield Wednesday boss Dave Challinor believes that Barry Bannan can "extend his career" if he deploys him in a deeper midfield role, but admits he is still experimenting with him across the midfield in the infancy of his time in the Hillsborough dugout.
  • The former Stockport County boss has had a very busy first couple of weeks at the helm in South Yorkshire, with games in three different competitions and a couple of massive league outings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield Wednesday boss Dave Challinor believes that Barry Bannan can "extend his career" if he deploys him in a deeper midfield role, but admits he is still experimenting with him across the midfield in the infancy of his time in the Hillsborough dugout.

The former Stockport County boss has had a very busy first couple of weeks at the helm in South Yorkshire, with games in three different competitions and a couple of massive league outings.

In those two third-tier matches against Plymouth Argyle and Barnsley, Challinor chose the same starting eleven, which saw Bannan move further forward to partner Callum Slattery, creating two 10s behind Davis Keillor-Dunn.

Against the Tykes, especially, he seemed to excel in that role, producing the kind of performance many expected Bannan to have already yielded this season. In truth, he's not been the Scotsman of old back at Hillsborough, but his free kick led to Jamal Lowe's opener, and he assisted the second, too.

In a recent development, that performance gives hope that the 36-year-old may still be key at this level, but Challinor feels that playing him further back could add years onto his career. Ultimately, it's a good conundrum to face.

Bannan demonstrated how he can still influence games further forward at Oakwell on Friday night, but the attacking midfield role will put more of a strain on what the veteran Scotsman can do, as it means he has to get up and down the pitch more often.

The Wednesday manager stated that, while his influence further forward could be useful, he could add one or two more years to his career by playing deeper and pulling the strings from there, something which Bannan has done throughout his time at Hillsborough.

It has been revealed that "I think Barry can play in different roles,” Challinor remarked, per the Star. "For how we want to play with control, him playing centrally and a tiny little bit deeper, because of his technical ability, I think will work really well.

"It will probably extend his career depending on how long he wants to play for because there'll be less demand on him to influence the game higher up, but he still has the ability to do that.".

Challinor admitted that it's a "luxury" to be able to have someone like Bannan who knows how to get into positions to influence games further forward, but knows that, right now, it's about experimenting with different players in different roles until Wednesday get to the January transfer window.

"I suppose the luxury we have at the minute is we're able to ask him to be a little bit more disciplined, but on other occasions let him go and be a little bit of a free spirit," he added.

Industry observers note that "When he's higher up, he can certainly do that. He can roll into wide areas. He can come deep if he wants. But we have to find, let's say, different things at the minute because we don't have the players specifically fit in the positions that we'd like to have.".

Since Challinor came in to replace Henrik Pedersen earlier this month, he immediately changed the shape to a back three, similar to what he played while at Stockport in their back-to-back third-placed finishes in the last two seasons, before an injury crisis in defence forced him to a back four towards the end of last term.

Evidently, he's gone for formation over personnel, and is experimenting with what roles each player can play in this structure before the January transfer window opens, where it'd be expected that more players who fit this formation can be bought.

That's led to Jamal Lowe playing at left wing-back in the last two league games, but that's also partly down to both Max Lowe and Reece James being injured, and Bannan playing a bit further forward than he has been so far, given how he can influence games.

It may be the case that Challinor wants to see how Jaden Heskey can impact things in the meantime, or if he feels that the other options behind the striker aren't at the level of Bannan or aren't fit enough to play, so he feels he has to play him there for the time being.

Either way, it's a good question to have, and by January, we may see the Scotsman back in a deeper role.

Extending his career at Hillsborough should be on Bannan's mind, as the midfielder edges ever so closer to the appearance record for the famous South Yorkshire side.

The win over Barnsley was appearance number 496 in a Wednesday shirt, putting him eight away from tying Alan Finney for fourth all-time.

Andrew Wilson sits first on 546, but current club captain Liam Palmer is behind him on 524 and could likely break that record this season, barring any injuries or other forced absences, so Bannan may have to play a little longer to overtake his compatriot.

Do you think Barry Bannan will end his career atop the all-time Sheffield Wednesday appearance charts? Let us know in the comments.

In a recent development, the Scotsman turns 37 in a week, so he will need to be managed properly if he is to make Wednesday history before he retires. Playing him a little deeper and making him control the game without moving around too much could be the key to doing so.

Challinor got Oliver Norwood to play that role perfectly in his final two years at Stockport. Bannan may be a little older, but he still has the capabilities to do just that.

Breaking: Charlie Austin drops 'downstairs toilet' claim about Millwall's away dressing room

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Den is widely regarded as one of the most intimidating stadiums in English football due to the atmosphere that the Millwall fans can generate, and it remains something of a throwback in the modern era.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charlie Austin compared the away dressing room at Millwall to a downstairs toilet due to how cramped it is.

The Den is widely regarded as one of the most intimidating stadiums in English football due to the atmosphere that the Millwall fans can generate, and it remains something of a throwback in the modern era.

Millwall supporters embrace that, and they pride themselves on how difficult they can make it for the opposition when they arrive in South Bermondsey.

However, it seems the club are also doing their part to make things tough for the away team, as Charlie Austin opened up on his experiences visiting The Den.

Speaking on the Chaz Kicks Off podcast, the ex-QPR striker discussed the different times he went to Millwall, as he also namechecked the players that could make it hostile, before sharing a light-hearted comparison of the state of the dressing room.

“I remember playing against Millwall for Swindon, when we got beat 3-2 on the final day. I was ****, and I was so nervous because I’d built it up in my head.

Sources indicate that “I went back there with Burnley, and we won 2-0, which wasn’t too bad. With QPR, we drew 2-2 and they scored right at the end, and I scored in the game.

“But, Danny Shittu, their centre-half, was as wide as the tunnel at Millwall, and he’s in there shouting, just trying to intimidate, so that’s when it starts. Then you had David Forde, the goalkeeper, he used to walk out last, which is unusual for a keeper, and he had a major presence about him, where you’d think ‘I wouldn’t want to catch a right-hander off him’!

It has been revealed that “They don’t do anything in the dressing room, other than, the only way I can explain it - Millwall’s away dressing room is the equivalent of your downstairs toilet! It is small, and it is tight. It’s what you expect.”.

This is nice for Millwall fans to read, as every football fan wants their team to make their home ground a difficult one for opponents - and the Lions have managed that.

Clearly, things are different now, as you won’t get players like Shittu shouting in the tunnel to intimidate the away team, but it’s a good story showing how football used to be.

It’s fairly common for the away dressing room to be worse than the home one, and, again, it makes sense, as you want the away team to feel as uncomfortable as possible without crossing the line.

So, this is a good insight from Austin, and it indicates what clubs will do in order to try and gain even the smallest edge to help them on the day.

Whilst The Den understandably has a reputation, it’s fair to say it hasn’t been the fortress it once was so far this season.

That’s not to blame the fans, as they’ve made it raucous, and the 2-2 draw at home to West Ham produced a brilliant atmosphere.

Industry observers note that will Millwall make the play-offs this season? Let us know in the comments below.

Yet, for whatever reason, Millwall have been inconsistent on their own patch, and it’s a key reason as to why they’re not in the mix for a top eight finish at the moment.

But, there will be a belief among Neil and the players that they can turn things around, and picking up wins at home will be pivotal if they are to start climbing the table.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.
  • Industry observers note that milan had a very clear initiative when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.

Industry observers note that milan had a very clear initiative when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack. Instead, however, it’s the underdog Cisse who has been running the show, while the Portuguese striker has been at the bottom in terms of output.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning (see image below), that’s why there cannot be – and likely won’t be – a Milan without Cisse in attack. Ruben Amorim now wants to build the attack around him, as opposed to introducing him every now and then.

Industry observers note that the most recent clash, the 2-1 win against Genoa, was a good example of this. Amorim went for a bold formation with Cisse, Ramos, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot together. A team with a lot of quality and an attacking-minded style.

It has been revealed that it was a shape that reminded us of 2009-10, when Milan were guided by another foreign coach: Leonardo. He chose a very attacking-minded side with four attackers and two midfielders, which is something that Amorim almost replicated.

Modric and Rabiot in front of the defence (Pirlo and Ambrosini then) and the fantasy project with Pulisic, Moreira, Cisse, and Ramos, comparable to the Ronaldinho, Pato, Seedorf, and Borriello of the old days.

Despite this, the goals were scored after two mistakes by Genoa (even if Milan’s pressing helped), so the goal is to repeat the experiment against Frosinone and to increase its effectiveness, the experiment should be repeated tomorrow.

It has been revealed that in that sense, Cisse will be important as he’s the top scorer: three goals in Europa League and five in Serie A. He has scored with both feet and his head, demonstrating a combination of talent and an eye for goal: characteristics that are very important for a team like Milan.

Sources indicate that the average also speaks for itself: eight goals spread across 658 minutes means he scores a goal every 82 minutes. Best of all, his versatility means that he can play as an attacking midfielder, a left-winger, and even as a centre-forward.

Industry observers note that at just 20 years and 17 days old, thanks to the fifth goal in his ninth Serie A appearance, Cisse became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone in the first ten games with Milan, at least since 1994-95. Only Pato did it younger, at 18 years and 181 days.

Furthermore, he’s one of only three players born after 2006 (top five leagues) to have scored eight or more goals in all competitions, along with Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner, who also scored eight.

As the pink newspaper concludes, Ramos has also produced eye-catching numbers, but in this case in a negative sense: 1,191 minutes on the pitch, three goals scored, meaning one goal scored every 398 minutes.

#175496. EFL club hit with unprecedented FA punishment – it's never happened before

EFL club hit with unprecedented FA punishment – it's never happened before

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (358 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Millwall have been handed a partial-stadium closure for their upcoming clash with Sheffield United in the EFL Championship, with the FA handing them an unprecedented punishment after ableist and homophobic chanting during their game with Charlton Athletic.
  • The chanting took place in the clash between Millwall and Charlton at the Den in January 2026 - a game that finished 4-0 to the Lions thanks to a late blitz of goals.
  • Official statements confirm that Millwall were in breach of FA Rule E21, which relates to a football club's responsibility to ensure its spectators and supporters (home and away) behave in an orderly fashion at matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Millwall have been handed a partial-stadium closure for their upcoming clash with Sheffield United in the EFL Championship, with the FA handing them an unprecedented punishment after ableist and homophobic chanting during their game with Charlton Athletic.

The chanting took place in the clash between Millwall and Charlton at the Den in January 2026 - a game that finished 4-0 to the Lions thanks to a late blitz of goals.

Official statements confirm that Millwall were in breach of FA Rule E21, which relates to a football club's responsibility to ensure its spectators and supporters (home and away) behave in an orderly fashion at matches.

Millwall have released a statement following the FA's punishment, where they have listed the sanctions they have faced for ableist and homophobic chanting towards Charlton.

Within that is confirmation that they have been handed a one-match partial stadium closure - the first time that an EFL club has been handed such a punishment from the FA.

The Athletic go on to confirm that it will be the Dockers Stand of the Den that will be impacted, with blocks 19, 20, 47 and 48 shut for the upcoming game against Sheffield United on December 8th.

That's going to impact a reported 1,274 fans who have tickets in that area, although they are invited to select an alternative seat in the stadium.

The additional one-match partial stadium closure that will be suspended until the end of next season will be activated if Millwall fans engage in more discriminatory chanting.

The statement from Millwall lays out what was chanted and why it was deemed unacceptable.

'South London S—' was the ableist chant, with 'You take it up the a—' the homophobic charge on the sanction.

Millwall's statement read: "Both chants are discriminatory and offensive, and the club condemns them in the strongest possible terms.

"Ableist and homophobic chanting, as well as any other form of discriminatory chanting, has no place in football or society. Any individual identified as engaging in such abuse will face the consequences.".

Millwall's next home game comes on November 28th when they host Burnley in the EFL Championship.

Bruno Fernandes has ended up on AC Milan’s radar ahead of the summer, according to reports, with a free transfer potentially on the cards.

Having just turned 32, Fernandes is still at a good age and he’s showing that with Manchester United so far this season. In 14 appearances, he has bagged six goals and three assists, so it’s no surprise that many clubs are monitoring his situation given the expiring contract.

Kevin Phillips names the 3 EFL clubs he's most worried about right now

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (816 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although the EFL Championship season is only 15 games old, former striker Kevin Phillips has outlined his current worries for three sides in the division at this moment in time.
  • The second tier of English football is renowned for pulling up plenty of surprises throughout almost every 46-game season, and no doubt many more are lying in wait in the coming months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although the EFL Championship season is only 15 games old, former striker Kevin Phillips has outlined his current worries for three sides in the division at this moment in time.

The second tier of English football is renowned for pulling up plenty of surprises throughout almost every 46-game season, and no doubt many more are lying in wait in the coming months.

At present, the top end of the Championship is extremely congested, with only eight points separating the 12 sides occupying places in the divison's top-half, with one of Phillips' many former sides, Birmingham City, currently leading the way on goal difference.

However, some are currently at risk of cutting themselves adrift when it comes to an unwanted relegation to League One, and it is fair to say that the one-time experienced forward, who is now a regular fixture on our television screens, has his concerns over multiple clubs in remarked situation.

Phillips, 53, enjoyed an esteemed playing career in both the Premier League and Championship, which included promotions from the division with all of Birmingham, Crystal Palace, Leicester City, Sunderland and West Bromwich Albion.

Netting 134 of his career goals at second tier level, the former striker knows exactly what it takes to be successful in the division both collectively and individually, as well as seeing the other side of the game at first-hand through an array of coaching and managerial roles.

Speaking to Football League World via Best Betting Sites, Phillips explained his worries over three clubs, two of which he has affiliations with in the form of Watford and Derby County.

"Well, there are a few, to be fair. A couple of my old teams I used to play for, and one I coached at," he said. "The team I'm most worried about, and the team where they shouldn't be, they should be a lot higher and doing better things, is Watford. I speak about them quite a lot.

Sources indicate that "I never know what to expect from them on and off the pitch, but history should suggest that they should be doing a lot better than what they're doing. So I fear for my old club. They've been in and around the relegation zone, avoided relegation, and I really fear for them this season," Phillips added.

"They might slip through. I really hope they don't, and I hope they find a bit of form, but I fear for them.

Phillips then discussed the situation at Burnley, with the Clarets in danger of becoming the third club in as many seasons to suffer successive relegations from the Premier League to League One.

"And of course Burnley as well, from where they've been to where they are now. The season they're having for such a big club, in the Premier League not so long ago, to be where they are now, having only won one game in the Championship," the former striker continued.

Industry observers note that "It's been really disappointing, so I'm worried for them. And I think Derby as well. I hope they pick up form. So two of my old clubs are in there, but Watford and Burnley for sure.".

Phillips broke through the Watford ranks, meaning it is no real surprise he has concerns over the Hornets at present given his attachment to the club.

Alessio Dionisi was drafted in as the 24th head coach of Gino Pozzo's ownership in June on a two-year contract, but after making an encouraging start 2-1 victory against high-flying Southampton on the opening day, it was downhill from there for the Italian.

Winning three games since and given the ownership consortium's reputation for firing-and-hiring saw intense speculation over another sacking come to the fore last month, and after Saturday's 4-0 loss to Sheffield United at Bramall Lane, Dionisi was sacked after just 18 matches in charge.

Many would also agree with Phillips' concerns over Burnley and Derby right now, with the two sides making up the bottom three alongside Preston North End after 16 games.

The Clarets have only defeated Watford so far this term, and in recent weeks, the vulnerability of the squad at Turf Moor has been laid bare for all to see.

Recent findings suggest that do you agree with Kevin Phillips, or are you worried about a different EFL Championship club? Comment below!

Nicky Hayen's tenure lasted just 14 games, with his final two outings seeing Burnley surrender leads against Wolves and Lincoln City, whilst Fabio Celestini's tenure has got off to a winless start.

The Swiss head coach admitted before the international break that his new chargers are certainly in a dogfight to preserve their Championship status after his side gave up a comfortable 4-1 lead away to Cardiff City to lose 5-4, with Kyle Walker issuing a similar stance after Sunday's compelling 2-2 draw with Blackburn Rovers in the East Lancashire derby.

Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg admitted that he "couldn't understand" how enormous the interest surrounding a football club in a specific town or city was before he came over to coach Boro last year.

The Swedish boss celebrated one year at the Riverside on Tuesday, and in that time, Middlesbrough have been transformed and look certain to be playing Premier League football in the near future.

Boro were inside the top two when Hellberg was hired, following the shock departure of Rob Edwards, but the brand of football he has instilled in the club has been thoroughly entertaining, both for fans of the club and neutrals alike.

Middlesbrough have a proud fanbase, and after years of Championship obscurity, they look to be on the rise again, and the energy surrounding the club from the fanbase is something that Hellberg has been surprised by during his first year on Teesside.

It has been revealed that kim Hellberg has seemed destined to coach in England ever since he started managing in Sweden a decade ago. But, as is often the case with foreign coaches, he was taken aback by the swell of support which surrounds football in this country.

Sources indicate that it's tribalistic at times, and the fact that smaller cities and towns can have such a loyal, large following is always something that first-time coaches in this country take as a surprise. Hellberg is no different.

Recent findings suggest that what's been your favourite moment from Kim Hellberg's first year in charge at Middlesbrough, Boro fans? Let us know in the comments.

To celebrate one year in charge at the Riverside, Middlesbrough ran a Q&A with their head coach, with him answering questions from fans. One such query regarded what has surprised him the most about Boro.

"I know football was everything here, but the biggest surprise for me was the enormous interest and energy around the football club," he said.

"How everyone feels like they care about Middlesbrough and live through that, how key football is wherever you go, wherever you are, football is everything here. I think I knew some bits were like that, but I couldn't understand how significant it was.".

Kim Hellberg will likely be referencing how most English clubs have such a passionate fanbase that lives through the team, but in Middlesbrough especially, that's evident.

According to recent reports, boro are a one-club town. No other professional team is in the Middlesbrough area, with the closest professional club being Hartlepool United, 13 miles away. Even then, those in Hartlepool count themselves more in County Durham, rather than Teesside.

Either way, it's a proud following at Boro, and has been for years. Their time in the Premier League grew that, but even in the past few years, attendances at the Riverside have hovered around the 25,000 mark in the Championship.

All you have to do is look at the numbers over the past year to know that Kim Hellberg is bringing back some of the supporter base who may have become a little disassociated with the club as they stagnated in the second tier, though.

According to recent reports, boro's lowest Saturday attendance this season was against Cardiff City, at 28,991. Their average attendance in the entirety of last season was 27,622, and the year before, in Michael Carrick's final term, it was 25,416.

Over 3,000 more fans are coming to watch this Middlesbrough team under Hellberg than they were in the final moments of the Carrick reign, which demonstrates how much bigger an already big support has been under Hellberg.

Hellberg went on to say that his dream as Boro boss was to bring the club back to the Premier League, which he hopes to do this season.

Middlesbrough currently sit atop the Championship table, and look good value for it, too. What's arguably more scary, though, is that they seem to still have a higher gear that they can reach, and if they can find it, they may win this league at a canter.

Sources indicate that then, the Swedish boss may end up being taken further aback by the extra support which will come at the top level. Boro are a club that has been starved of Premier League football, with this being the 17th of the last 18 seasons they've spent in the Championship.

You get the feeling, though, that if Hellberg can get this side into the top flight, they'll stand a greater chance of staying there than they did under Aitor Karanka a decade ago.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the substantial screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Sources indicate that had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

Industry observers note that what a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

In a recent development, the lack of discipline in their ranks was exposed when Dan Burn scored a late consolation and ended up in a melee with James Tarkowski and Joelinton. But the issues Jaissle, who lamented that “we must improve”, has to correct are for another day: this contest belonged to Everton.

Recent findings suggest that thierno Barry had provided the finish that secured a trip to Fleetwood in December and what an opportunity it is for Moyes to make Everton semi-finalists in this competition for the first time since 2016. Whether Grealish will have a part to play in it remains to be seen.

Thierno Barry with Everton's third! 🔵 https://t.co/dyb8fKud8N.

The last thing Everton needed on a night of such importance was a distraction. Grealish will have a tough job mending relations, particularly with Moyes, but there was a paradox: though he had caused a major issue for 90 minutes he became an irrelevance.

Moyes is impatient to give Evertonians a big day out and his only focus was on crossing this hurdle – for all that Newcastle have had a turbulent start to the campaign, they are dangerous opponents and you wondered in the fraught opening 30 minutes if they might exacerbate the hosts’ woes.

As Jaissle hopped and squirmed on the sidelines, imploring Newcastle forward, chances came and went: Harvey Barnes had a header saved, Fabian Schar tested Jordan Pickford from 30 yards while Vitalii Mykolenko and James Tarkowski made huge goal-saving challenges.

“We should have scored more goals,” Jaissle, who was dressed as if auditioning for the role of The Milk Tray Man, growled. “It [losing] was shocking as the game was not that bad.”.

Moyes was infuriated by Everton’s initial inertia, so much so there was a point when the Scot prevented Merlin Röhl, his own full-back, from taking a throw-in until Tarkowski and Jake O’Brien had complied with his gesturing to get 10 yards further forward.

Sources indicate that it might have looked old-fashioned but it worked. Suddenly Everton started asking questions, Hayden Hackney almost got on the end of a cross from Mykolenko, and it encouraged the supporters on the vertiginous South Stand to raise their voices and become more involved.

Industry observers note that what they needed was a goal to set things alight and in the 34th minute, it arrived. Tyrique George won possession by Newcastle’s corner flag, the ball dropped at Hackney’s feet and he instinctively ushered it on to James Garner, who whipped a right-footed drive beyond Lukáš Horníček.

Recent findings suggest that james Garner puts Everton in front against Newcastle in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 https://t.co/TzponbWyGU.

In a recent development, the roar that greeted it was a mix of elation and wonder, relief and desperation. The locals have grown weary of seeing nights with potential end in disappointment but here was the foothold they craved and the opportunity they were ready to seize. Soon the lead would be doubled.

Industry observers note that hackney would score the goal, converting a super Barry cross, but let us acknowledge the fabulous refereeing of Farai Hallam, who waved play on when he might have whistled for a foul on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall. And how Everton took advantage.

Hayden Hackney doubles Everton's advantage! 🔵 https://t.co/VIY0Iln3nI.

It must be remarked the officiating this week has, in the main, been outstanding. Watching a match without the persistent spectre of VAR has been liberating and you can see the referees have felt free to make decisions on instinct.

Industry observers note that the whole experience of knowing a contest cannot be re-refereed has been better for all. It will not catch on, sadly, because too many people have gone too far down the road with VAR, but we should embrace the purity of “old school football” while we can.

Evertonians – the Prime Minister included – certainly embraced the buffer of a second goal and the fact Hackney scored it also felt like a throwback: a player who was plucked out of the Championship in the summer and encouraged by Moyes to show he could make the next step up.

Recent findings suggest that he did that and so, too, did Everton, their progress was assured in the 69th minute when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall dashed down the left and crossed for Barry to finish. Moyes puffed out his cheeks as it hit the net. He, more than most, deserved to enjoy this one.

  • Around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel.
  • The footage revealed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

Around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel. The video offered supporters an early glimpse of Mauricio Pochettino working with his new squad, but its release quickly raised concerns about the privacy of United’s training sessions.

The footage revealed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

After backlash from fans over the breach of privacy, the video was removed on Friday morning, with the operator issuing an apology for filming the session.

In his statement, the operator said the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He remarked: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”.

The operator apologized directly to the club, its new head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”.

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

Recent findings suggest that “Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”.

It has been revealed that manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a substantial reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in important matches.

“A recurring issue with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of significant trophies.”.

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in major games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

In a recent development, “Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”.

Pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

The Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

Mauricio Pochettino has made it clear he wants to be involved in Manchester United’s major squad decisions, while also addressing questions surrounding captain Bruno Fernandes ahead of his first game against Liverpool.

The newly introduced Manchester United head coach explained that he wants to have a voice in decisions that shape the squad.

“Sometimes maybe you are a coach and maybe you have more power in the decisions,” Pochettino stated in his first Manchester United press conference.

“It depends on the structure, it depends on the communication, the relationships, you know, with all the areas.”.

Mauricio Pochettino highlighted his responsibilities are clear about who he selects and plays in games.].

“I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, and I’m going to pick the team, I’m going to make the changes, and of course in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad.”.

Pochettino was also asked about Bruno Fernandes, whose critical comments about Michael Carrick’s tactics became a talking point during the former manager’s final weeks at Old Trafford.

The Argentine was really keen about the squad’s commitment, dodging the blame on Fernandes and describing Fernandes as a key figure in the dressing room.

“The commitment from all the players was amazing from day one,” he said.

“Bruno is our captain and a very vital player but all the players need to feel they are important from the bottom to the top.”.

Pochettino revealed that he had already spent time speaking with the players to understand their situation both on and off the pitch.

“Yesterday we spent three hours chatting to the players in my office and maybe I missed the injured players.”.

Pochettino admitted the first few days at United had been extremely busy as he tried to get up to speed before his first match.

He is excited by the opportunity but knows there is little time to prepare for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

“It’s a happy time but at the same time, so busy,” he explained.

“It’s been about adapting in the last few days, and it’s a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool in the game on Sunday.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea.
