📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

That matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

In a recent development, that number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

According to recent reports, 🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F.

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the notable detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

In a recent development, gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

In a recent development, alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

That is where the Kante reference lands with force. Chelsea do not need Gusto to imitate Kante’s position. They need him to absorb the same professional standard: repeat actions, clean defensive choices, no wasted emotion and total commitment to the collective rhythm.

In a recent development, the Marco Palestra deal changes the right side of Chelsea’s squad immediately. Read Chelsea has already examined how Palestra’s arrival offers a tactical clue over Alonso’s defensive plans, and that pressure is now sharpened by market noise around Gusto.

Chelsea can frame the situation in two ways.

One is profit-led. If a club comes close to the reported £75million level, selling a player signed from Lyon for a much lower fee becomes a powerful PSR lever.

The other is football-led. If Alonso sees Gusto as a high-upside wing-back who fits his model, selling him just as the coaching environment becomes more suitable would carry long-term risk.

Manchester United have spent approximately £95m appointing and dismissing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, according to BBC Sport, with the total expected to pass £100m following Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.

United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.

The figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis. That total is expected to rise once the costs of Michael Carrick’s dismissal and appointing Pochettino’s coaching staff are included.

Pochettino signed a two-and-a-half-year contract on 13 November, replacing Carrick after a difficult start to the Premier League season. The club’s Stock Market filing states that the appointment fee will be recognised in its financial accounts for the current quarter. United also confirmed borrowing a further £10m on 16 November, taking the amount drawn on their revolving credit facility to £240m.

Sources indicate that pochettino is United’s ninth full-time managerial appointment since Ferguson’s departure, including Ralf Rangnick’s interim spell. The club have also changed managers during each of the past three seasons.

Industry observers note that united’s financial disclosures show that their long-term debt stood at £577.4m on 30 September, while outstanding transfer-fee commitments totalled £417m. Those figures are separate from the cost of appointing and dismissing managers.

A Reuters analysis has put the wider cost of managerial and senior football staff changes above £100m, using a broader calculation. Pochettino now faces the task of improving United’s results, beginning with Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool.

Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.

The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.

Thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad. However, this raises questions as to why some England supporters have turned on the defender after he has continued to perform well for Arsenal.

The answer lies with the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

Recent findings suggest that white left the England World Cup camp in November 2022, returning home due to personal reasons. The FA confirmed that White will not return to the squad and asked that his privacy be respected.

He did not play in the first two group games for England and missed the last group game against Wales due to illness.

There were reports that White had fallen out with assistant manager Steve Holland, but neither the FA nor England management confirmed this was the reason he left.

Gareth Southgate later stated there were no problems between White and Holland and that White had simply withdrawn himself from selection after the tournament.

This meant that White would never play for England again while Southgate was still manager. Some fans were clearly upset by this, as they felt White was shunning his country.

Recent findings suggest that when White returned under Tuchel in March 2026, he was met with a negative reaction. He was booed by the crowd when he scored his first-ever international goal against Uruguay. White was also booed in the same fashion against Japan.

Sources indicate that he has since explained that supporters might view the situation differently if they knew the full story. However, he has chosen not to reveal the private details behind his departure.

Tuchel has shown little concern about White being affected by the controversy.

The England boss said after the win on Thursday that he had not heard any boos and praised White’s qualities, work ethic and desire to play for his country.

He believes White can help England win games and added that he has the backing of the coaching staff.

Arsenal fans will be unsurprised to learn that White is still a valuable asset for Mikel Arteta, offering defensive consistency and being able to play as a right or centre-back.

The bad press that White is receiving from England fans will not go away any time soon. However, he has not done anything to hurt his reputation at club level. The reasons why he left for the World Cup are personal.

Industry observers note that the main focus for Arsenal will be getting him match fit again. As for the England fans, we shall see.

Bruno Fernandes himself has now confirmed that the club have offered him a newly introduced contract, but the midfielder has made it clear that he does not want discussions about his future to become a priority right now.

“If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here,” Fernandes remarked.

The Portugal international added that he could have earned considerably more by accepting offers from other clubs, but always chose to continue his career in Manchester.

Fernandes revealed that discussions initially took place towards the end of last season and continued when the players returned for pre-season.

However, the United captain believes the current situation at the club makes it the wrong time to focus on his personal future.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side,” he explained.

“I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.”.

Industry News: Chelsea Could Claim Share of £164m Compensation

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years.
  • Reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision.
  • The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

Industry observers note that this matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

It has been revealed that according to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

In a recent development, manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

Recent findings suggest that “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

That statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

It has been revealed that data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Recent findings suggest that within that total, London clubs are noted to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

Prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

For Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a major boost. It could help fund new signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

Industry observers note that city chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

Chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

It has been revealed that jamie Gittens has withdrawn from the England Under-21 squad. He suffered an ankle injury during Tuesday’s qualifier against Kazakhstan at Molineux. The Chelsea winger left the ground on crutches. He has returned to Stamford Bridge, where the Jamie Gittens injury will now be assessed by the club’s medical staff.

Gittens picked up the knock after a challenge during the second half of England’s win over Kazakhstan. He was withdrawn as a precaution. He did not take any further part in the match. England have been careful not to overstate the glitch and no further reports have come out further.

The 21-year-old struggled to put weight on the affected ankle and was seen limping around Molineux after full time. That prompted an immediate release back to his club, rather than any attempt to assess him further in camp.

England Under-21 boss Lee Carsley addressed the injury directly after the game. He confirmed the nature of the knock and the decision to send Gittens home.

“Jamie got a kick on his ankle,” Carsley said after the match. “We never take any risks. With the age of these players, we don’t ever keep them in camp to see how they are. He will go back.”.

England’s statement on the squad changes, detailed in a report from Football.London, confirmed the wider fallout from the fixture.

Sources indicate that “Mukasa’s call-up follows the withdrawal of Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Norwich City pair Kellen Fisher and Ben Chrisene through injury,” the statement read. West Ham midfielder Divine Mukasa has been called up as cover for all three.

It has been revealed that gittens has been an unused substitute in every Premier League fixture Chelsea have played this season, with his only two appearances under Xabi Alonso coming in the Carabao Cup. Those minutes have offered him little platform after his big summer move.

According to recent reports, alonso’s squad selection has been a talking point since he took charge. Our earlier look at Xabi Alonso’s squad choices at Stamford Bridge covered how competitive things have become. An ankle injury will not change his pecking order in the short term. It does, though, remove any chance of him pushing his case this week.

In a recent development, chelsea’s break has brought other headlines too. Cole Palmer also withdrew, for entirely different reasons, after his recall by senior boss Thomas Tuchel to the full England squad. Chelsea will be watching both returns closely before domestic football resumes.

Industry observers note that chelsea have not yet issued a formal update on the severity of the injury. Any recovery timeline will depend on an assessment by the club’s medical team once Gittens is back at Cobham. Nothing beyond the crutches seen at Molineux has been confirmed.

According to recent reports, given his limited game time this season, the immediate concern is less about missed fixtures than a setback to his integration under Alonso. Fans can follow how the squad shapes up before the next fixtures through our recent line-up updates. Further news on Gittens is expected once Chelsea’s medical staff finish their evaluation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United players have reportedly been told to expect a further increase in training demands under Mauricio Pochettino after Sunday’s Premier League match against Liverpool.

The upcoming manager arrived at Carrington on Wednesday following his departure from the United States national team and has had less than four days to prepare for his first match in charge. According to The Sun’s report, published on Saturday evening, United’s players have already noticed longer and more intense training sessions compared with those under former manager Michael Carrick.

Recent findings suggest that the newspaper reports that Pochettino has initially concentrated on introducing his tactical approach, with more demanding physical work expected once the Liverpool fixture is over. An unnamed source claimed the players had already felt a significant change in tempo and workload, despite the Argentine having only a limited period to work with the squad.

Pochettino is also reported to have taken a hands-on approach during training, regularly stopping drills to explain his instructions directly to players. The report adds that the 54-year-old has been communicating in English with United’s staff and has asked his predominantly Spanish-speaking coaching team to do likewise.

Pochettino’s first assignment is Sunday’s visit to Anfield, with United looking to improve on a difficult opening to the Premier League season. The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager conducted an extended training session on Saturday as preparations for the fixture continued.

However, the reported emphasis on fitness and conditioning suggests that his wider changes at Carrington may become more apparent after the Liverpool match. United have not publicly confirmed the details of the training programme described in the report.

Today’s game kicks off at 4.30pm GMT.

  • Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roma have put an £86m (€100m) price tag on Manu Koné, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, reviving the Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link that first emerged over the summer. Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

In a recent development, “There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”.

In a recent development, D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

It has been revealed that “Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I stated it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of vital players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”.

Chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

Koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

For now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

Sources indicate that nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

Liverpool v Manchester United: Five classic wins at Anfield

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readmanutd

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.
  • With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.
  • United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Recent findings suggest that fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

According to recent reports, sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Industry observers note that diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Recent findings suggest that forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Recent findings suggest that few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

With a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

It has been revealed that liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

According to recent reports, those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

Sources indicate that the 20-year-old has made a blistering start to his Serie A career and attracted interest from a number of Premier League clubs after his impressive displays so far. Arsenal are reported to be interested.

The Gunners are among several clubs, including Brighton, keeping tabs on the player, according to Italian football news website Tuttomercatoweb. The striker is rumoured to be worth up to 60 million euros. That’s an eye-watering sum for a player who is just starting out in his professional career.

Cissé was signed by Milan from Hellas Verona in February 2026 but was allowed to finish the season on loan at Catanzaro.

Prior to joining the San Siro, he had already showcased his potential with six goals in 22 games in Serie B. He has made a huge impact since moving up to the top division.

This indicates that Milan is considering his future, rather than looking to make a profit. It also demonstrates just how quickly his reputation has developed.

Arsenal have the funds to target exciting young talent, but would they want to spend so much on Cissé?

There is no indication that he would be an instant replacement for Arsenal’s current attacking options. However, Cissé’s age, goal-scoring ability and versatility make him an interesting prospect.

This could be one to keep an eye on beyond January. Milan have little motivation to sell, and Arsenal might want to see how he develops before committing themselves.

Cissé has already hit the ground running in Italy and now needs to prove that his initial success can turn into something more consistent.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute.
  • According to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

In a recent development, pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the new head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

According to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

The Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

According to recent reports, the defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical plan was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

Nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

United return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the problems exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

Pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

Sources indicate that for Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

Recent findings suggest that the Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

Industry observers note that according to Sky Sports, United intend to challenge the decision, with Isak’s chances of regaining possession central to the dispute. Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

“To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he said, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher stated.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. Yoro remains eligible for Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting, before attention turns to a crucial domestic fixture for Pochettino’s side.

Recent findings suggest that frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Industry observers note that arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

According to recent reports, arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

Sources indicate that but Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

London City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some newly introduced energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

Industry observers note that the Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

But Rice has played in a more advanced position on the right-hand side of the midfield duo this season, and this has not limited his impact but instead highlighted another key part of his game.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

Industry observers note that this is of particular interest, as he has often come under criticism for his distribution. But he is averaging nearly double the amount of line-breaking passes he did last season.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a new contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

The reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding new ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.
  • It has been revealed that the departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect.
  • The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

It has been revealed that the departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.
  • The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.
  • According to recent reports, however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

According to recent reports, however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

In a recent development, “The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino remarked.

It has been revealed that “Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”.

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

It has been revealed that “But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

The FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

  • The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 03:43 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:45 EST, 24 November 2026.

Merseyside Police reportedly arrested seven supporters at last weekend's clash between Manchester United and Liverpool, with two on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.

But even before the visitors saw Leny Yoro sent off and four conceded without reply, this fixture has long been one of the most incendiary in the top flight.

Supporters arrested for suspected tragedy chanting are thought to be a 63-year-old man from Heywood, Greater Manchester, and a 57-year-old man from Wallasey, in Wirral, as per the Athletic.

Both clubs have waged independent battles against tragedy chanting, which sees fans taunt opponents by mocking major disasters, such as Hillsborough, the Heysel Stadium disaster, and the Munich air disaster.

Some tragedy chants are even aimed at the personal lives of players on the pitch, and in 2024, latest guidance from the Crown Prosecution saw tragedy chanting upgraded to a criminal offence.

Seven people have been arrested following Man United's trip to face Liverpool at Anfield (police pictured breaking up a fight in the away end).

As well as tragedy chanting, a 47-year-old man from Swinton, Greater Manchester, was arrested on suspicion of possession of a class A drug.

Two men - a 49-year-old from Didsbury, South Manchester, and a 38-year-old from Denton, Greater Manchester - were arrested on suspicion of indecent and racialist chanting.

A further two, aged 30 and 23, were arrested during the final minutes of Sunday's clash as a skirmish broke out among the away supporters at Anfield.

But despite the enmity between the two teams, there were a greater number of arrests last month, when Man City visited Anfield for the first match in the wake of the revelation that the club had been found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them for breaching the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

That fixture saw 10 fans arrested, with five arrested on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The match-up between the two sides became increasingly charged with the establishment of a rivalry at the top of the table under former managers Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola.

In 2018, the Man City bus was attacked with bottles, bricks and flares ahead of a Champions League meeting between the two sides, with future fixtures in Liverpool at times seeing the players' bus route amended to avoid throngs of home fans.

In March 2025, Merseyside police requested an unorthodox kick-off of 3.45pm for the match, rather than the customary Sunday start time of 4.30pm, in a bid to reduce issues between the two sets of fans.

  • Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.
  • Industry observers note that storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history.
  • Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Industry observers note that storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

Industry observers note that he was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

According to recent reports, storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

Sources indicate that he played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

In a recent development, he will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

It has been revealed that just over one year ago, West Ham’s Finlay Herrick was stepping out on loan for Boreham Wood in the National League – the fifth tier of English football. A far cry from London Stadium yesterday as he replaced Mads Hermansen in goal and made his Championship debut, apparently hearing about his impending start just on the morning of the game.

And despite the first half concession from the corner, Herrick did a pretty fair job with excellent double saves later in the game and some assured glove work catching the ball – which had seemed like a lost art at times in the last couple of years.

Herrick after his unforgettable FA Cup penalty shootout debut last year.

This was a massive gamble by Scott Parker which could have backfired dreadfully. With no Areola, the temptation must have been to revert to Hermansen yet the Hammers’ head coach stuck with his instinct. After the first half goal concession, Parker must have wondered – briefly – whether he’d made a huge howler.

Has Herrick done enough to keep his place? It seems Parker is dead set on replacing Hermansen so until Alphonse Areola is ‘fit and ready’ then Herrick should be prepared for more pitch time. He certainly has the ambition:.

“I hope this is the start. I hope I’ve done myself justice and proved to the fans that I don’t just want to be third choice, I want to be playing, I want to get back to the Premier League and be part of that”. (whu/youtube).

Describing the competition amongst the trio of goal keepers, Herrick was quick to praise Hermansen for the encouragement and help he’s received recently, describing the three keepers as a team more than individuals fighting amongst themselves for the sole starting spot:.

“There’s one goal keeper shirt and there’s three of us – but we’re like a band of brothers and we always stick together, me Mads and Fonz- no matter what. “.

Difficult to believe Herrick is still only 20 – he seems to have been around West Ham’s fringes for ever- but he joined the academy at six years old and looks to have the talent to go all the way. From yesterday’s solid start, he didn’t let his manager or his team mates down and should feel rightly pretty proud of himself.

The question for Scott Parker is whether he continues between the sticks at Fratton Park on Tuesday night.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As I left the London Stadium to a chorus of boos, I found myself desperately searching for positives from a frustrating 1-1 draw against the league’s bottom club.

Sources indicate that the first was the performance of Alvarez. Largely cast into the shadows through the stubbornness of our former manager, he grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck. He took control, lifted the crowd, and, above all, displayed the leadership qualities this team has lacked for much of the season.

In a recent development, the second positive was that the statistics backed up what I’d watched unfold on the pitch. West Ham dominated possession with 79%, registered 30 shots, and recorded an xG of 3.13. The problem? Only four of those efforts were shots on target.

It has been revealed that we gifted Preston their opening goal. It came from a calamitous mix-up, with Piroe’s flicked header looping backwards onto the crossbar before dropping kindly for Liam Lindsay to tap home from close range. It could be argued that Herrick should have been more commanding from the corner, but he made amends later with an excellent double save.

There were concerns that we wouldn’t pull one back, we did on the 60th minute, Mavropanos heading home his sixth goal in 15 league appearances this season.

“Ifs” and “buts” don’t win football matches, and as Parker noted afterwards: “The overall performance suggests we should win. The fine margins of football are, and the reality is, if Tomas Soucek scores that last-minute goal, it’s probably a different interview.”.

For me, I’m not going to be negative. We needed a win and we didn’t get the three points, but what I want to see now is the team build on the domination, the chance creation and the shot volume by going to Fratton Park on Tuesday and getting the job done. If we concede first there and deliver an abject performance, then and only then will there be more serious questions to ask.

Taken in isolation yesterday’s team performance at London Stadium doesn’t look quite so poor: A draw against the bottom side who had just beaten promotion prospects Southampton symbolises everything good about this Championship: Predictable it is not.

West Ham hit the wood work four times and on another day could easily have romped home. Trouble is, after the losses and draws of recent weeks a solitary point does nothing to halt the downward slide. It does seem a little early to start demanding change to Parker’s starting eleven – who as a unit were paying together for the first time yesterday.

Nuno was ‘the tinker man’ and you’d hope Scott Parker will persevere, despite criticism and articles today demanding the immediate axing of key players.

Piroe scored on his debut – surely it is a little early to consider discarding the striker who needs a run in Parker’s side.

Footballfancast.com is typical in calling for Joel Piroe to be dropped after his poor game:.

“The left-footed attacker delivered a dismal display in the centre-forward position and must be dropped by Parker ahead of the trip to Portsmouth in midweek”.

The real problem with that knee-jerk reaction is that there is, simply put, nobody else to fill that role: Castellanos was invisible yesterday and fluffed his one chance, a header at the far post that didn’t get within a yard of the target. Pablo is, to all intents and purposes, finished now that his benefactor Nuno has left and until January, the cupboard is bare unless Parker gambles all on one of the youngsters.

Piroe needs the same kind of run which Castellanos had in the team before discarding him: He’s already outscored the Argentine forward by 4 goals to 1 this season. Give him a break.

#175412. West Ham’s Answer Was There All Along – So Why Ignore It?

West Ham’s Answer Was There All Along – So Why Ignore It?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (784 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United’s lack of cutting edge against Preston North End was concerning, but perhaps the most frustrating aspect of Saturday’s 1-1 draw was that Scott Parker already appears to have the answer to the Hammers’ creative problems.
  • At the risk of sounding like a scratched record, West Ham have an emergency, break-glass solution to breaking teams down.
  • What’s particularly puzzling is that I genuinely believe the best we’ve seen Bowen play in the last couple of years came during the second half against Cardiff City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United’s lack of cutting edge against Preston North End was concerning, but perhaps the most frustrating aspect of Saturday’s 1-1 draw was that Scott Parker already appears to have the answer to the Hammers’ creative problems.

At the risk of sounding like a scratched record, West Ham have an emergency, break-glass solution to breaking teams down. It’s called Jarrod Bowen, and I’m not entirely sure I’ve ever seen our captain play wider than he did at the London Stadium yesterday.

What’s particularly puzzling is that I genuinely believe the best we’ve seen Bowen play in the last couple of years came during the second half against Cardiff City. On that occasion, Parker was effectively handed a blueprint for getting the best out of West Ham’s most crucial player, yet we’ve barely seen it since.

During that extraordinary second-half comeback against Cardiff, Bowen was given a certain amount of freedom, perhaps encouraged by Parker or maybe he just took it upon himself to drift into the middle of the pitch and cause havoc.

Whatever the reason, he had a hand in all three West Ham goals, and the difference was remarkable.

For the first, he drifted into what might be regarded as the number 10 position and chipped a lovely ball over the Cardiff back line for Divine Mukasa to finish.

The second was similar, with Bowen again creating the opening from a central position. His pass found Joël Piroe, whose flick released Arne Engels to score.

The third goal saw Bowen back in his more familiar position on the right-hand side, where he supplied a wonderful inswinging cross for Max Kilman to equalise.

Jarrod Bowen was given license to roam against Cardiff.

It has been revealed that but that only went to show quite how much freedom Bowen had. In essence, he was everywhere.

As a blueprint, Scott Parker couldn’t have been given a better gift on his first day in charge than discovering that West Ham’s best player could operate with devastating effect from a free role.

Indeed, I was so encouraged by what I saw that I subsequently wrote about how Scott Parker must restore West Ham’s most dangerous weapon following the defeat at Blackburn.

Because for a brief period against Cardiff, it looked as though we’d stumbled upon something rather special.

Therefore, I was a little underwhelmed that we didn’t see it repeated against Blackburn and very worried when we probably saw our captain more straightjacketed than ever against Preston North End.

If I could offer Parker one piece of encouragement or advice, it would be to get the best out of Bowen.

I’m quite sure our latest head coach will improve the defence, and I think we saw signs of that yesterday, albeit against the league’s worst team.

But it can’t come at the expense of shackling our best player, who potentially could only be here for a few more months.

As I argued in my assessment of the Preston draw, West Ham had plenty of possession, shots and territory, but very little magic.

And that’s the really bloody annoying part. We have a player who can provide exactly that, but we’re asking him to operate in a way which makes life considerably easier for the opposition.

I know one thing. If I was head coach of an opposition Championship team and I saw Jarrod Bowen shackled to the right wing, I’d breathe a huge sigh of relief.

Because West Ham get one shot at this.

If we don’t succeed in getting promotion, Bowen could leave for a pittance of £15m. That’s the release clause in the revised contract he agreed following relegation.

We do know that Bowen flew to Prague to meet Daniel Křetínský before pledging to remain at West Ham for another season, as he explained in his interview with Sky Sports.

And I’m now very fearful that we are going to waste what should really be something of a cheat code for the division.

Industry observers note that bowen is comfortably our best attacking player, and we’ve already seen how devastating he can be when allowed to roam. Yet rather than building upon that discovery, Parker appears to have returned him to a position where he’s easier to mark and less able to influence the game.

I wish it weren’t so, but I’ve now come to the conclusion that the second half against Cardiff was a pure accident rather than a window into what we could begin to see from Scott Parker as he got his teeth into the West Ham job.

But decisions like that could well make the difference between automatic promotion and a play-off place, if we’re lucky.

24 hours on from West Ham’s  tepid point against the bottom side in the league and whilst the justified criticism is flying around, there are definitely positives to pull out of a fixture in which West Ham dominated all the important statistics save the most important one: The points tally at the final whistle.

Sadly, again the Hammers have lost ground on the leaders and now sit eight points adrift. And yet, from Scott Parker’s comments, there are definite signs that he’s learned from at least some of the mistakes made by his predecessor. Reversing Nuno’s decision to cast out Edson Alvarez from the senior team proved a massive success.. Who knew.

Yesterday’s re-integration of ‘El Machin’ into the starting line up was his first league appearance in a West Ham shirt since May 2025.

This was an Alvarez playing more like his first season as a Hammer.

As Scott Parker summed up, Alvarez did not let him down:.

“He brought every bit of what we needed. It’s a young team, and his experience today in terms of organising and his general presence on the pitch was very, very good for us for large aspects.

Sources indicate that “It was a big ask and I knew that going into the game, he hasn’t played at all this year and probably hasn’t had a lot of training in and around the first team. But I just felt his experience and know-how around it was needed, and for sure he was a massive part today of why we performed the way we performed” (Justin Allen- YouTube).

The Mexican clearly cares: He was in tears before kick off, so tough has his time in the football wilderness been.

Industry observers note that having been such a critic of him during his card-strewn Lopetegui era, credit where it is due. Edson Alvarez was, indeed, excellent yesterday and it is a testimony to his professionalism that he played a full ninety after not playing competitive football since August.

If he can maintain that kind of focus and form, Parker may well have found the missing piece in West Ham’s defensive jigsaw puzzle, that proved beyond his predecessor who simply wouldn’t extend the olive branch to any of his ‘frozen out’ players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Preston North End, the bottom side in the Championship, arrived in east London yesterday unaffected by the occasion and kept West Ham at bay for an hour until Dinos Mavropanos headed equaliser restored parity and saved Scott Parker’s blushes.

Two weeks’ work during the international break had accounted for very little as Preston withstood everything the Hammers and their almost 60,000 fans had to throw at their lowly opponents.

Sources indicate that and therein lies the problem. Having surrendered the small, intimidating, sometimes downright hostile atmosphere of Upton Park back in 2016, the distance from the pitch and the wide open spaces of the Olympic Stadium are about as intimidating as a day out at London Zoo for our opponents and their fans who continue to pour scorn on the venue.

It just doesn’t strike fear into opponents as it should. Even when we score.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium – as our opponents are finding out.

Preston fan Tm Mercer, writing in the Lancashire Evening Post, makes it abundantly clear that there was no noticeable crowd reaction to lift the home side, as there should have been once Mavropanos restored parity:.

“Aside from play-off finals, I’m pretty certain it is the first time I’ve been in a stadium for a league match with 60,000-plus through the gate.

Sources indicate that yet, when they equalised, it did not feel like the roar of that many people in such a cavernous ground. Give me somewhere like Gigg Lane, stood in their paddock pitch side, any day!”.

For the uninitiated, Gigg Lane is the home of Bury FC with a capacity of around…..12,000.

Nobody is suggesting the Hammers fans were silent. The cursèd accoustics from the soulless bowl and sheer distance from the pitch play right into opponents’ hands. And, ten years after moving in, it’s going to take a lot more than some safe standing and a couple of family zones to fix it.

It has now been revealed that Newcastle United are set to host 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup matches.

The United Kingdom was officially confirmed as the tournament’s host nation on Monday.

The Newcastle United Women’s team official social media declaring that the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is: ‘Set to be the largest single-sport event ever staged in the UK, the bid features Newcastle among the host cities.’.

Newcastle United Women’s star Jordan Nobbs: “Having grown up in the North East, I know how much football means to people here and just how passionate the fans are about the women’s game. The FIFA Women’s World Cup coming to the UK in 2035 is another milestone for our sport, and bringing matches to this region would take the tournament to another level. We’ve seen what happens when the Lionesses play in front of crowds up here – the atmosphere is electric.”.

Jordan Nobbs adding: “Hosting these matches wouldn’t just be an incredible celebration of football; it would inspire the next generation of young girls across the North East by showing them that the biggest stage in the world is within their reach.”.

BBC Sport state: ‘The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James’ Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.’.

They then add: ‘Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland. Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men’s Euros in 2028 after the UK government mentioned in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time – but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035. A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham’s new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.’.

I don’t think any Newcastle United fans should be taking too much from this announcement with regards to whether or not a new stadium will be built, rather than redeveloping St James’ Park.

A new stadium could be built in time to host matches at the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

Whilst the club could also withdraw from hosting any games in these next few years and their fixtures given to one or more other stadiums.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that football is often described as a results business, but every now and then the underlying statistics tell a completely different story to the league table.
  • Using BBC Sports match stats data, over our last five matches, the Hammers have registered an astonishing 111 shots, with 35 of those efforts hitting the target.
  • Those are numbers you would normally associate with a Championship elite attacking side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that football is often described as a results business, but every now and then the underlying statistics tell a completely different story to the league table. Right now, West Ham United are providing one of the most puzzling examples of that phenomenon.

Using BBC Sports match stats data, over our last five matches, the Hammers have registered an astonishing 111 shots, with 35 of those efforts hitting the target.

Those are numbers you would normally associate with a Championship elite attacking side. To put it into perspective, averaging more than 22 shots per game and seven on target suggests a team consistently creating chances, putting opponents under pressure and spending large periods on the front foot.

All too familiar expression of Hermansen anguish.

During the same five-game period, West Ham have conceded just 19 shots on target. That points to a side that is not only attacking effectively but also controlling matches overall defensively yet there have still been some major lapses in defence, which has led to conceding “sloppy” goals – 12 in total!

So despite posting overall metrics that would not look out of place among title challengers, West Ham have failed to win any of those five games!

Industry observers note that having watched four of those five matches, the answer seems fairly clear, goalkeeping and costly mistakes at the back have been the biggest contributing factors. While only scoring 8 goals from those 35 shots on target suggests major improvements up front is required!

According to recent reports, against Preston, Herrick was required to make just one save but still conceded, despite the visitors registering only two shots on target. Piroe contributed largely towards their goal.

Compare that with Mads Hermansen’s recent run.

At Ewood Park, Blackburn managed just three shots on target but scored twice, with only one effort being saved.

Cardiff recorded four shots on target and found the net three times, with Hermansen making a single save.

It gets worse when West Bromwich Albion visited the London stadium and had three shots on target, they scored with all three, and Hermansen was unable to make a save.

Southampton generated seven shots on target and scored three goals. On that occasion, Hermansen acquitted himself better, making four saves, but the pattern remains clear, opponents have been converting a remarkably high proportion of their chances.

The data suggests a team that should be winning far more matches than it is.

Which brings us to the obvious question:.

According to recent reports, what’s going on at West Ham? How can a team produce 111 shots, 35 on target, concede only 19 shots on target, and still fail to win a single game in five matches?

Sources indicate that tomorrow’s trip to Fratton Park is the first time West Ham have faced their south coast opponents in the league away from home since 2012. The Hammers have the advantage of the bragging rights from a solid 3-1 Carabao Cup victory back in August but the Pompey side who they come up against tomorrow night is likely to look very different from that which succumbed at London Stadium.

According to Sportsmole, Portsmouth manager John Mousino has significant challenges all over the pitch:.

“Portsmouth’s lengthy absentee list features Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, Luke Brooke-Smith, Keshi Anderson, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Benjamin Arthur and Connor Ogilvie.

Jayden Meghoma is a doubt after being forced off in the closing stages against Bolton with an ankle problem, while a calf problem prevented Marlon Pack from starting Saturday’s draw.“.

Scott Parker will face the dilemma over whether to continue with Saturday’s centre-back pairing of Morato and Mavropanos, Maximilian Kilman now available once more having served his suspension.

Fans will be divided over the return of Max Kilman for Portsmouth: Will Parker gamble on Morato?

Similarly, retaining Finn Herrick in goal will be something of a gamble but one that most fans will hope Parker takes as the young ‘keeper made saves on Saturday that Hermansen has failed to do in the four games preceding Saturday’s draw.

There are no good options for West Ham’s manager with Castellanos so out of sorts and Pablo unlikely to make the squad.

Josh Ajala looked so good the last time these two sides met that there’d be a temptation to at least name the home grown talent  for the bench, especially considering the little-known Championship requirement for a minimum of seven English players to make up West Ham’s match day squad.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Redknapp has been talking about Newcastle United.

The Sky Sports pundit reflecting on Saturday at St James’ Park.

An ultimate game of two halves.

Newcastle United unrecognisable after the break, when compared to the opening 45 minutes.

Interesting to get a neutral perspective on what occurred, what changed.

Jamie Redknapp declaring on Sky Sports: “I think first half for any player in that Newcastle team that would have been a lonely place, because you were getting played off the park, the spaces seemed so big and your home crowd have been booing you. You’re like, ‘this is going to be a really tough [second] half’.”.

Recent findings suggest that jamie Redknapp: “Matthias Jaissle made three great changes. Elanga added pace, Livramento good energy down that right-hand side, and Ramsey was one of the best players on the pitch. Newcastle United, full respect from me, I thought they revealed a great deal of effort and they played against a very difficult side in Arsenal, but they got after them. It just highlights you what a bit of energy can do.”.

The home fans had been as out of form, lacking the necessary zip and energy, as their team had been before the break.

In a recent development, jamie Redknapp: “And once that crowd get up and you get that first goal, anything was possible. And they will look at that second half thinking, actually, we could have won this game. Really good performance from Newcastle. I would give Jaissle more credit because he’s taken a lot of stick. It’s been really hard for him, but he’s definitely got some money in the bank tonight. He will be proud of his team. The fans will be proud of their team. And they made it very difficult for Arsenal that second half.”.

I am not always his biggest fan but that is an excellent summary for me, of what we all witnessed on Saturday.

Jamie Redknapp also looking at the 2-2 draw from the Arsenal perspective: “You are getting so much time on the ball [in the first half]. Declan Rice was able to turn. Bruno Guimaraes had so much time in the first half and then all of a sudden Jacob Ramsey comes on and he is all over you. He is closing you down. Myles Lewis-Skelly is getting put under pressure and that was full credit to Newcastle. The fundamentals that you have to do to win a football match by winning second balls, by putting teams under pressure, by getting in people’s faces, Newcastle did well in the second half.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The manner in which some players depart West Ham along with the bad feeling that develops as they press for a departure on their own terms can sometimes be the lasting memory that tarnishes their whole stay in east London.

Such was certainly the case of Marco Arnautovic, for example, a successful forward who demanded a new deal, got everything he wanted, and then quit anyway.

However, with some players, despite the bitterness, the rancorous ending of their career fades in the memory over time, and their stay is regarded more fondly for the highlights rather than the bad blood generated at the close.

Not quite sure yet which category the career and departure of Lucas Paqueta will fit into as his stay at West Ham thankfully fades into the dim and distant past.

Infuriating, gifted, inconsistent, yes, but forever remembered for ‘that’ pass to Jarrod Bowen in June 2023, Paqueta’s ‘yellow cards for bets‘ two year saga became, sadly, the other defining memory of his three years as a Hammer.

Winning the conference League title was his career pinnacle – until last weekend when he finally achieved ‘the ambition of a lifetime‘  (huh) with his boyhood club Flamengo.

Looking on the bright side, West Ham fans don’t have to endure the ‘baggage’ that came with Lucas Paquetá.

As reported by sportwitness.co.uk, West Ham’s former number ten referred merely to his time in England as ‘two very difficult years’ en route to winning the Brazilian league title:.

““I went through two very difficult years in my life. I decided to come back because I wanted this feeling, I wanted to feel welcomed, to be at the club I love.”.

“I have no words to describe what I’m feeling. I arrived at this club when I was eight years old. My biggest dream was always to win trophies wearing this shirt.”.

Sources indicate that well done, Lucas. We’re all very happy for you.

According to recent reports, it feels a bit like learning an ‘ex’ has got remarried. Good for them. So what? I’m so over them now….

In these days of instant access to everything, fame is sudden and success is apparently supposed to happen overnight. Criticism of West Ham’s team and their mid-table mediocrity is often swift and harsh. Even players who arrived in the summer are already being written off, according to supporters and news sites.

Which seems especially harsh considering the age and trajectory of several key players in this West Ham side.

How many ‘West Ham legends’ of the past would have been discarded after their first dozen games, I wonder, if they’d not been an immediate sensation.

Bad enough that so-called ‘fans’ took to booing Scott Parker’s very first home game at 90 minutes: Now it seems one of the youngest talents from the summer intake is already being labelled as a  ‘flop’.

That’s the flavour of a report out this evening from givemesport.com who claim that:.

In a recent development, as they take aim at ..Edwin Austbø who, at just twenty one, has hardly had a chance to get settled in east London before he’s being labelled a’ massive money’ (eh?) flop, despite his transfer fee being a modest £11 million. Perspective being everything, that’s about a quarter of a Kilman who cost £40 million and would surely be most people’s choice for the ‘big money flop’ label.

A flop? After three months? With two goals and two assists at just 21 years of age, I’d say Austbo is well on track to grow into the team.

“Expectations were also high that summer signing Austbo could prove to be an exciting addition in the second tier this term….He has two goals and two assists for the Irons so far this term, but you would probably expect his goal contribution numbers to be higher in a team which has scored 38 league goals…..

As things stand, Austbo is promptly becoming a big-money transfer flop, and he needs to improve quickly to start repaying his fee.”.

Industry observers note that steady on, guys, This young man has huge talent, was not outrageously expensive and has already produced more goals and assists than players who cost twice his transfer fee. At least wait until the end of the season – his first in the English leagues – before writing him off.
