📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With David Raya out, Kepa Arrizabalaga has a great chance to prove that he is more than just an Arsenal cup keeper. Mikel Arteta needs to have confidence in his number two. He needs to ensure that he upholds the same high bar set by the starting keeper as Borussia Dortmund come to the Emirates.

Raya has been ruled out of tonight’s Champions League game following a shoulder problem which he picked up in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle United.

Whilst the initial diagnosis is good news, surgery is not required. Further tests will determine Raya’s recovery period.

In a recent development, as previously mentioned, Kepa will be stepping in for Raya at St James’ Park. Moreover, Arteta has stated his preferred choice of player in this situation. It seems that Illan Meslier will miss out on the opportunity to play this time.

In a recent development, as well as playing for Arsenal, the Spaniard has formerly played in the Champions League for Chelsea and Real Madrid. He has already appeared 14 times for the Gunners. Including in the league stage match which saw them beat Kairat Almaty.

Industry observers note that whilst Kepa has typically been second choice to Raya, his game time has mostly been in the EFL Cup. He will now need to prove himself as a trustworthy option for Arsenal should Raya be injured or otherwise unable to play.

As well as being a good goalkeeper, Raya is also good at passing and positioning. This in turn assists Arsenal in attacking from the back line.

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson has acknowledged the quality that Spanish goalkeepers have at creating good defensive and central positioning. This can frequently be an under-recognised yet crucial component in Arsenal’s build-up play.

Like Arsenal, Kepa will also have to remain calm when playing out from the back. Although Kepa does not necessarily need to replicate all of Raya’s qualities, he will need to have good decision-making skills as well as good communication.

According to recent reports, meslier is still in contention, having played in the Carabao Cup game against Fleetwood Town. Kepa has been Arsenal’s number two keeper in the Premier League and was able to rush on in for Raya when he was substituted at Newcastle.

It does seem that Kepa is the obvious option, and he can further cement his position in Arteta’s team.

Arsenal’s schedule is demanding. They are playing Manchester City on a Sunday and there are also worries about Raya’s fitness. So far, the club has not yet received medical information on Raya’s status.

In a recent development, then there is Dortmund. They have already secured victories in their first four games in the Champions League and are level on points with Arsenal in the league section.

Kepa does not have a great deal of flexibility. Arsenal require the newly introduced goalkeeper to offer them security.

In case Raya needs more time to recover, it is necessary for Arteta to be able to guarantee that there is an effective replacement.

For Kepa, it is equally an opportunity to prove that he can assume this leadership position for the team during important moments.

  • Sources indicate that west Ham dominated possession and registered 30 attempts against Preston, yet never really looked clinical enough to score the winner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Portsmouth v West Ham United EFL Championship, Fratton Park, Tuesday 24 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT.

This is a crucial match for West Ham and Scott Parker, who has probably endured the shortest honeymoon period of any Hammers manager in recent memory. His first three games have produced a rousing comeback against Cardiff City, a forgettable defeat at Blackburn Rovers and Saturday’s frustrating 1-1 draw with Preston North End.

Sources indicate that west Ham dominated possession and registered 30 attempts against Preston, yet never really looked clinical enough to score the winner. Indeed, had the referee awarded another 20 minutes of injury time, I’m still not convinced we would have found a second goal.

Sources indicate that parker is still waiting for his first victory as West Ham head coach, and Tuesday’s trip to Fratton Park represents another difficult assignment. Portsmouth have lost just once in eight Championship matches and sit only one point and two places behind the tenth-placed Hammers.

It has been revealed that ordinarily, one might expect Parker to do some tinkering after failing to beat the team at the bottom of the division. However, I suspect he won’t make sweeping changes because he was very pleased with the way his team performed against Preston.

Edson Alvarez – likely to become key in Parker’s intends this season.

Sources indicate that parker stated he got almost everything he wanted from the performance apart from the result, while describing Finlay Herrick and Edson Álvarez as “brilliant” in his post-match assessment. I’m not quite sure I would agree with that overall verdict, although the return of Álvarez was unquestionably a bonus.

It has been revealed that the Mexican looked decent on his return to the team and provided some much-needed protection in front of the back four. Parker has probably made it clear that, for the remainder of this season, West Ham will play with a recognised holding midfielder.

Sources indicate that without wishing to sound like a scratched record, I still believe Jarrod Bowen needs to be used more centrally. Parker appeared to have been given the keys to unlocking West Ham’s attacking potential against Cardiff, but unfortunately he seems to have kept them in his back pocket ever since.

Bowen remains our most dangerous attacking player, yet watching him pinned to the right flank against Preston was depressing. West Ham lacked magic, invention and somebody willing to take responsibility in the areas where matches are won.

Mohamadou Kanté can consider himself unlucky not to have featured at all against Preston because he has been one of West Ham’s better players this season. There is an argument for playing him in the attacking midfield position at Portsmouth, where his pace and direct running could give Parker’s team something different.

However, I don’t think Parker will throw the baby out with the bathwater. He has already spoken about remaining stable and consistent, so I expect Divine Mukasa to retain his place behind Joël Piroe.

According to recent reports, piroe should continue up front, as much because of the lack of convincing alternatives as anything else. Manor Solomon could return on the left, with Parker perhaps deciding that his experience is better suited to a difficult night at Fratton Park.

I suspect there will be a change at left-back, with Ollie Scarles coming into the team. Max Kilman is available again after completing his one-match suspension and should immediately return alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos.

Sources indicate that according to the club’s official team news, Alphonse Areola and Kyle Walker-Peters continue to be assessed. Unless Walker-Peters is unexpectedly declared fit, Joël Veltman should remain at right-back.

Sources indicate that portsmouth possess a worse attack than West Ham but a better defence, so this is unlikely to be an open game. They are only two places and one point behind us, while their recent results suggest Parker’s team will have to work extremely hard for anything at Fratton Park.

In a recent development, west Ham’s failure to convert possession into goals remains the obvious concern. However, if Parker can keep things tight defensively and finally find a way to make one of our attacking opportunities count, I believe the Hammers can edge it.

Portsmouth 0-1 West Ham United.

Pat Nevin discussing Newcastle United.

This follows Saturday’s game against Arsenal.

Plenty of angles to look at and debate from a very eventful 90+ minutes.

Plus of course all of the subplots that swirled around this Newcastle United v Arsenal fixture.

Pat Nevin sees a lot of Newcastle United, the former Chelsea and Everton winger a regular visitor at St James’ Park.

He was on media duties this weekend as well.

Reflecting back on his latest visit, Pat Nevin detailing in the Football Extra newsletter: “I nipped down to a freezing St James’ Park at the weekend, where the reception for their beloved former midfielder Bruno Guimaraes made the weather feel positively balmy. Hell hath no fury like a Geordie scorned, but fortunately the home side played so well in the second half that, at one stage, they forgot to boo him for a good two whole minutes.”.

Pat Nevin adding: “I understand why football fans feel this way. Having lost Antony Gordon, Alexander Isak and Sandro Tonali already, it was a heavy blow to lose the one who mirrored their passions the most. Players think differently. The idea of turning down the English champions, who could win the Champions League, and instead stay at a club that is shipping out all of the best talent around you, is demanding an unthinkable level of loyalty. Most would substitute loyalty for stupidity in that sentence.”.

I suppose that also sums up my many decades of following Newcastle United, especially when non-football fans ask me why I do it….

Back to Saturday’s match though and Pat Nevin: “Arsenal were fabulous and the gulf between the teams looked enormous in the first half but the comeback after the break could well be my favourite 45 minutes of the season so far. From nowhere, Newcastle bullied, dominated, outran and even outplayed Arsenal. It was glorious stuff. Now comes the tough part as manager Matthias Jaissle has to recreate that feeling every week.”.

As Newcastle United fans,, what will our stupidity/loyalty be rewarded with in the weeks and months to come?

At the same time, a gutsy point at Brighton followed by home wins over Man U and the Mackems, then the world will feel a very different place.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that tonight’s mid table clash, yep, 10th play 12th, brought back memories of a West Ham United game in Division 1 back in 1992/1993. Without wanting to sound like Paul Whitehouse’s legendary Fast Show character, Ron Manager, and his famous cry of “jumpers for goalposts”, my mind drifted back to the footballing world of the 1990s this morning.

According to recent reports, I recall watching the game on ITV, on a programme called the London Match, hosted by Ian St John, and a quick search on YouTube found some footage, with Greavsies side kick being  joined by Glenn Hoddle. Jim Rosenthal was at Fratton Park as part of the commentary team.

Portsmouth featured in the FA Cup semi finals the previous season. West Ham drew 1-1 with Derby County the week before the game, Trevor Morley cancelling out a clearance by Mitchell Thomas which had cannoned off Ludo for an own goal earlier in the game, which kept the Hammers in the top six.

Bonzo was the West Ham manager in 1992.

With Billy Bonds at the helm, West Ham were unbeaten in six games, yet faced a Pompey team that had only played twice at home, won both and not conceded. They boasted the prolific striker Guy Whittingham up front, and with Jim Smith in the manager’s seat, were stiff opposition for us. Yet as he stated in the warm up the Hammers were one of the favourites to go up.

Pre game the major news was welcoming back Julian Dicks our skipper who came off a three match ban.

The Hammers took the lead just before half time with Clive Allen (main  pic) scoring, yet despite an onslaught of the Pompey goal in the second half they couldn’t add to their tally.

Trevor Morley was denied by the woodwork, while Martin Allen (who was never afraid to shoot from distance) also had a long effort saved.

Happy memories, as it was a time when the club had a greater connection to us, the fans.

I’d settle for a clean sheet and a win tonight, how football has changed or as Ron stated “Isn’t it, wasn’t it, marvellous”.

A ten million transfer fee justified the move in most fans’ minds, but there was still a sense of unfulfilled promise, despite Potts’ finally achieving his dream of a Premier League debut for the team he loved and had supported as a child.

In a candid interview today with BBC.co.uk, Potts reveals why he chose to quit West Ham United.

Without putting too fine a point on it, the whole move to Belgian Champions FC Brugge came about through manager Nuno Espirito Santo’s selection choices and Potts being sidelined, as he explained:.

“In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren’t as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and noted ‘let’s explore options because this season I’m 22, turning 23’,” Potts said.

“It’s a massive part of my career and I wanted to play.”.

Nuno’s decision to limit Potts’ game time led to his decision to quit the club.

Subsequently the interest from Brugge- now competing in the Champions League against the likes of Liverpool this very week – arose and Potts grabbed at the chance:.

“The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn’t really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

Recent findings suggest that “I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.”.

And who can blame him: Freddie lines up against Liverpool this week in the Champions League – the same week in which his old club head for a second division mid table scrap with Portsmouth. Good decision young man. Go and win it.

Industry News: A disappointing end to a disappointing match for Newcastle United Women

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coming into the Newcastle United Women game with Nottingham Forest, both sides knew they were already eliminated from the Subway Players cup, so it was perhaps always going to be something of a ‘Dead Rubber’.
  • But with an international break looming it was still a chance for some players to stake a claim for a starting berth when the action resumes.
  • It has been revealed that forest made a raft of changes with Grace McEwen and Ebba Hed joining the ever-present Hannah Coan in central defence, with the trio forming a near impenetrable barrier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coming into the Newcastle United Women game with Nottingham Forest, both sides knew they were already eliminated from the Subway Players cup, so it was perhaps always going to be something of a ‘Dead Rubber’.

But with an international break looming it was still a chance for some players to stake a claim for a starting berth when the action resumes.

It has been revealed that forest made a raft of changes with Grace McEwen and Ebba Hed joining the ever-present Hannah Coan in central defence, with the trio forming a near impenetrable barrier. Both Codie Thomas and the rapid Deanne Rose operated on the flanks to great effect and caused United problems throughout.

They went with a midfield three of Rachel Rowe sitting in front of the impressive and hard working pair Georgia Brougham and Tove Almsqvist. While Norwegian Tuva Espas and the on loan Lois Shooter partnered one another up front and looked lively.

Newcastle United Women made some subtle changes with Kayla Rendell coming back in goal, while Jemma Purfield returned to the back four. Mollie Lambert was given a chance to play in her favoured central midfield berth while Beth Lumsden shifted over to the left wing to accommodate Leanne Kiernan, who was starting against her former side.

Photo by Adam Mackman via The Mag.

Newcastle enjoyed the majority of the possession but clear cut chances were few and far between, with any opportunities that were created seemed to be snatched at or fired over the bar.

According to recent reports, the Lady Mags created a couple of opportunities early on, with Beth Lumsden and Lois Joel going close. Before Jordan Nobbs was denied by the impressive Hannah Coan inside the area with a crucial block. Nobbs had another chance soon after, but her effort from a tight angle out wide was claimed by Forest goalie Georgie Ferguson.

Forest were creating chances of their own though. Codie Thomas put the ball into the box from the left, but Tuva Espas was unable to steer her header on target. However, they were soon ahead and with it the game changed over a four minute passage of play.

A speculative cross from Canadian international Deanne Rose out on the left was aimed at picking out Tove Almqvist but it flashed across goal and looked to be ushered out by Kayla Rendell. The goalie, on-loan from Manchester United, let the ball go past her as she assumed it was going wide of her far post, only to look foolish when the ball actually crept in off the woodwork.

It has been revealed that despite that setback Newcastle United Women responded well and from the ensuing kick-off were almost back level. Beth Lumsden playing on her less favoured left flank sent in a deep cross which was headed wide by Lambert.

But moments later Forest doubled their lead, when Tuva Espas forced a turnover in the United half and, spotting Rendell off her line, lobbed a perfect shot over the stranded goalie and into the net from 40 yards out.

Forest could have been three goals to the good before the break as Rachel Rowe worked the ball into the box, but was unable to find the final pass.

Newcastle had a lot of work to do in the second half but it was Forest who were looking the more dangerous side. Tove Almqvist played a ball over the Lasses defence as she tried to pick out Espas in the box, but Rendell was just able to gather it first.

It perhaps should have been 3-0 to the East Midlands side when a brilliant move was started by captain Georgia Brougham. She played the ball into Rowe who in turn found Espas, with the Norwegian international able to advance down the right before sending a great ball in for her strike partner Lois Shooter. However, United captain Rachel McLauchlan got there first and sent her clearance onto the post and very nearly into her own net before it bounced clear to safety.

According to recent reports, forest continued to create chances after that. Rowe curled an effort from the edge of the area and Rose continued to be a nuisance on the wing as she carried the ball with confidence into the final third and won a free-kick. Then did excellently to keep hold of the ball before playing it into the centre circle, to substitute Aimee Claypole, but she sent her effort straight at Rendell.

Claypole, who was on loan at Durham a couple of seasons ago, missed another chance after Freya Thomas played the ball into her feet. Her effort took a deflection before being collected once again by Rendell. Rose had another chance in stoppage time but could only find the side netting.

In a recent development, there were very few clear cut chances in the remainder of the game with Jordan Nobbs perhaps going closest when forcing Ferguson into a low save. Codie Thomas was also strong defensively and prevented another Newcastle shot. While Purfield fired over the bar from close range before sending a corner into Ferguson’s hands.

On what was a frustrating day for Newcastle, one bright spark was the introduction of Jessie Gale who ran her socks off after coming on, putting the Forest backline under rare pressure. The youngster’s cross/shot forced Ferguson into a save to preserve her clean sheet.

With just seconds left of stoppage time frustration began to tell and when Lois Joel shot into the net after the referee blew his whistle she was shown a yellow card, which then turned to red for dissent.

A disappointing end to what was a disappointing day.

Newcastle United: Kayla Rendell, Rachel McLauchlan (c), Hanna Németh (Aoife Mannion 88), Jemma Purfield, Kaitlyn Torpey, Lois Joel, Mollie Lambert (Jessie Gale 54), Jordan Nobbs, Beth Lumsden (Emilia Larsson 67), Martha Thomas, Leanne Kiernan (Kathleen McGovern 54).

Subs not used: Anna Tamminen, Hildur Antonsdóttir, Oona Sevenius, Gemma Evans, Abbie Richardson.

Nottingham Forest: Georgie Ferguson, Codie Thomas, Grace McEwen, Hannah Coan, Ebba Hed (Abbie Lafayette 89), Deanne Rose, Georgia Brougham (Freya Thomas 72), Tove Almqvist (Cerys Brown 89), Rachel Rowe, Tuva Espas (Aimee Claypole 62), Lois Shooter (Shania Hayles 61).

Subs not used: Katie Cox, Lucy Carney, Melissa Johnson, Lily Stevenson.

Where that leaves Newcastle United Women.

Industry observers note that the League Cup has adopted a Swiss League format for fixtures, with only the top eight teams of 23 progressing to the quarter finals. Both Newcastle and Forest were already mathematically eliminated before this game so the result matters very little.

Sources indicate that if you ignore the games played against WSL 1 sides Aston Villa and Everton, then Newcastle have conceded five goals in all competitions this season with four of those coming against Forest, who like United are still unbeaten in the league. That suggests the Lace City side should be one to look out for in the second half of the season, as along with Sunderland, they are the best side to face the Lady Mags so far.

A final concern was the standard of officiating for this game. With this being a clash between two second tier sides and a premier competition, surely the standard of the referee and assistants should be better than using ones from the local Non-League circuit. There are plenty of top female officials in the top tiers of the women’s game so surely both Newcastle and Forest deserved better? A referee who needlessly sent off a player in the 94th minute and his flag waving buddies who struggled to keep up with the play throughout the game, simply isn’t good enough.

Newcastle only have one WSL 2 game remaining before the Christmas break, against Watford on Sunday, 20th December.

Recent findings suggest that there is now an international break before an FA Cup Third Round tie away to Manchester Unity on the 13th December with the host team based in Chadderton, Oldham. The Lasses faced the same opponents in the cup back in November 2023, winning 9-2 away from home on that occasion. But following the game both sets of fans developed a great likeness for one another with many Newcastle fans supporting Unity in their games over the past three years.

The following Wednesday sees Newcastle bring their League Cup campaign to a close with current leaders Manchester United set to visit St James’ Park for a rare midweek game under the floodlights.

Just for a change one of West Ham’s young signings is being lauded rather than slated today – Edvin Austbø came in for a fair degree of stick in a report yesterday claiming he was heading towards ‘flop’ status – but the club’s pursuit and purchase of Dan Cummings from Celtic last summer is being complimented by his new manager.

Cummings went out on loan this month to fifth tier Aldershot Town and came off the bench to score within six minutes of his debut, as we covered yesterday.

As reported this afternoon by insidefutbol.com, The Shots’ manager Scott Davies has been waxing lyrical over Cummings and West Ham’s shrewd purchase of their future star:.

“Aldershot Town boss Scott Davies has admitted that he can see why West Ham United invested heavily in Daniel Cummings, following the former Celtic talent’s promising start to life at the National League side:.

“To bring on someone like Dan’s quality on with sort of half an hour to go, or 25 minutes to go, and then he gets a goal within five minutes is like a dream world for me as a manager.

“And for us as a management team, that takes the pressure off.

Recent findings suggest that listen, he’s been great in training and you can see the quality he’s got. No wonder why West Ham bought him for a lot of money. So, we’re really lucky to have him on loan and hopefully we’ll see more of him in weeks to come.”.

£600,000 in Aldershot’s world is a lot of money indeed for a teenager: For West Ham a mere drop in the ocean but good to hear that Cummings is making all the right moves.

Hopefully, the start of a stream of good news coming out of Hampshire as the young Scot finds his feet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goncalo Ramos has struggled to find the back of the net with the AC Milan shirt so far, with the Rossoneri hoping that he will eventually find his groove.

In a recent development, after years of struggling in the No.9 position, following the departure of Olivier Giroud, Gerry Cardinale stated enough is enough and spent over €70m on Ramos this summer. However, at least so far, it seems that wasn’t the right solution after all.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese striker has only scored three goals for the Rossoneri so far, despite featuring in every single game except one. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse has eight goals to his name and cost almost ten times less than the No.9.

Recent findings suggest that as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, if we were to conduct a survey today, Ramos would be the undisputed leader of seasonal flops for many. The fact that Milan are even considering investing another €50m+ in another striker states a lot.

According to recent reports, of course, such a move shouldn’t be seen as the Rossoneri demonstrating their lack of confidence in the striker. On the contrary, since Cardinale wants to aim for the Scudetto, having two very strong strikers would only be natural.

Still, Ramos needs to step up his goalscoring either way. The hard work he puts in every game, while recognised by the fans, isn’t enough as the usual “that’s not what a striker should do” always follows that praise. The old cliché is true: for strikers, scoring goals is the most key thing.

Industry observers note that as the pink newspaper continues, given their characteristics and quality on the ball, Edin Dzeko is a good precedent for Ramos to cling to. The Bosnian arrived in Rome from Manchester City and struggled a bit in his first season (eight league goals), causing a headache for everyone involved.

However, in the following season, he bagged a whopping 29 league goals with the help of Luciano Spalletti’s trust and the assists from Francesco Totti and Mohamed Salah. His resurgence was remarkable, so it’s something Ramos can take inspiration from.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that so where do Manchester United go from here? It is never a good look when opposition fans start willing a rival club to stick with their manager, but that was the ignominy that had befallen Michael Carrick by the end of an afternoon in which Lisandro Martinez’s latest plastic hardman impression embodied the very worst of United’s self-sabotage.

After seeing their team go 2-0 up when Cole Palmer converted the penalty given away by Martinez’s lunacy, the Chelsea fans taunted Carrick with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and later “You’re going down with the City”, a nod to the other Manchester club who are crisis torn for very different reasons.

According to recent reports, as the final whistle loomed, though, and with United just grateful Estevao had not punished Martinez’s red card more severely, the Chelsea fans had changed their tune. “Michael Carrick, we want you to stay,” came the chant from the Matthew Harding Stand and that cut far deeper.

And to think that the opening 45 minutes had offered United and their fans some hope of a little respite from the storm before ultimately giving way to an ever-darkening gloom.

According to recent reports, carrick, who had been given a stay of execution in midweek, stated he still expected to be in charge for Roma’s visit to Old Trafford on Tuesday in the Champions League. But it is hard to escape the feeling that another managerial change will be coming at United before too long even if no one can be sure what happens next.

Sources indicate that equally, the prospect of more upheaval in the dugout might elicit little more than a shrug from fans pointing the finger squarely at the ownership and the executives they have appointed. The players were spared this time but Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers remained the target of sustained abuse as did Jason Wilcox, the director of football.

Industry observers note that defeat here extended United’s winless run to nine matches, their worst sequence for 38 years. They have taken just four points from the last 21 on offer in the Premier League and seem to be sinking fast. Carrick was asked about the team becoming mired in a relegation battle. This is the territory United are in.

Industry observers note that the strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

Industry observers note that the problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Sources indicate that take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

Michael Carrick said he expects to be in charge of Manchester United next week despite Lisandro Martinez’s moment of madness leaving the club mired in a relegation battle and on their worst run for 38 years.

United were urged to sell Martinez after the controversial Argentina defender was sent off for elbowing Wesley Fofana as Carrick accused his side of “unravelling” as they slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

It left United without a win in nine matches, their worst run since 1988, and at risk of being sucked into the relegation zone. They have won just two of 13 games this season.

Industry observers note that the Old Trafford hierarchy gave Carrick a stay of execution in midweek and, when asked if he expected to still to be at the helm when United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, the head coach replied: “Yes. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.”.

Sources indicate that having been booked moments earlier for a foul on Morgan Rogers, Martinez was sent off for a second yellow. The incident came less than three weeks after the Argentinian was fined and publicly apologised for attacking United director of football Jason Wilcox and the board over transfer policy and was the latest in a series of mistakes from him on the pitch this season.

Joe Cole, the former Chelsea and England forward, believes United must get rid of Martinez.

Recent findings suggest that “Whatever the next Manchester United looks like, Lisandro Martinez has run his course,’ Cole stated on TNT Sports. “He’s at the scene of the crime too often for Manchester United and is at fault for moments and goals like that. So that’s probably his time done.”.

Carrick refused to publicly criticise Martinez but admitted his dismissal was a “huge moment” and felt his team “unravelled” in the second period.

“Things have gone against us in a significant way,” the United manager said. “It’s unravelled swiftly. There’s a lot of emotion right now. It’s a huge moment in the game. Sometimes you get setbacks in games and you’ve got to deal with that better. I’ve not seen it [the Martinez incident] back so I don’t know if it was [a red card] or not. He’s gone to it and the referee gave that decision, but it’s a big moment.”.

Asked if there would be a stigma attached to United potentially dropping into the relegation zone, Carrick added: “Not for me, no.”.

And when asked how his players would deal with a relegation battle, Carrick added: “We’ve got to keep moving forward and winning games. There’s no words I’m going to explain to you now that makes any difference, it’s not going to change it. We’ve got to move forward and win matches.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 16:02, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 16:14.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has explained why Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch are missing from the squad to face Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League clash.

Neither Dutchman was included in the Liverpool starting lineup or bench for the visit of the Red Devils, after also not being seen arriving at the team hotel on Sunday morning.

Gravenberch was already known to be carrying a heel injury, but Gakpo's absence came as a surprise, as the attacker was not name-checked in Iraola's pre-game fitness upgrade.

However, speaking to Sky Sports ahead of kickoff, the Liverpool boss revealed that Gakpo picked up a calf injury during the international break and is yet to return to team training.

According to recent reports, "Gakpo got injured with the Netherlands, he left the game with a soleus injury," Iraola stated. “He hasn’t been training with us, nothing since getting injured from the national team.".

Regarding Gravenberch, Iraola did not rule out a comeback for the midfielder against Club Brugge in Wednesday's Champions League clash, adding: "Ryan has been training but still is managing the pain.

“With Ryan we are going day to day – some days he can. We have been waiting until the end but he was in pain yesterday. Let’s hope we can recover him for the next one.".

Gakpo's absence is particularly damaging for both the Dutchman and Liverpool, as he has scored more Premier League goals against Man United than any other team.

Indeed, Gakpo boasts five goals from seven previous top-flight games against the Red Devils, scoring in each of his last three Premier League outings against the 20-time English champions.

Only against West Ham United (7) has Gakpo scored more goals against across all competitions, four in the Premier League and three in the EFL Cup.

Iraola did not disclose the severity of Gakpo's calf injury, which could be grouped into one of three categories; a Grade 1 mild strain, a Grade 2 mild tear, or a Grade 3 complete rupture.

If Gakpo has got away with the least serious calf problem, the Dutchman should only miss a maximum of two weeks, and he could potentially return in time for the Merseyside derby next weekend.

However, Gakpo is expected to sit out Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge, and a Grade 2 injury could sideline the former PSV Eindhoven man for the rest of the calendar year.

A Grade 3 tear would likely rule Gakpo out for around three months, putting him at risk of missing games against Inter Milan, Man United, Arsenal and Everton between now and February 6.

James Pearce reports that Gakpo has avoided a serious issue, though either Ngumoha or Victor Munoz should be given the nod from the first whistle against Club Brugge.

Vitalii Mykolenko delivered a dismal display as Everton were smashed 4-0 by Brentford in London on Monday.

Keane Lewis-Potter scored two goals within two minutes to hand the home side the lead in the first half, before Vitaly Janelt and Fabio Carvalho added the third and fourth against the 10-man Toffees after the break.

James Tarkowski was controversially sent off just before the break for a high challenge, despite having comfortably won the ball.

Monday's performance will certainly go down as a set-back for Everton, who had started the season excellently.

The Toffees had been on a run of three consecutive wins across all competitions, and will now face the visit of Liverpool on Sunday.

Moyes will have a key decision to make on Mykolenko, who certainly did not advertise his quality on Monday.

Mykolenko signed a newly introduced contract in June, and has been a key part of the Everton back-line for several years now.

And Moyes clearly trusts him, with the Ukraine international essentially a guaranteed starter when he is fit.

But Monday was a clear example of what the 27-year-old can leave Everton without on the left.

Mykolenko completed just 76 per cent of his passes, misplacing seven and completing only three into the final third.

He did not create a chance, take a shot or even deliver a single cross into the penalty box - an astonishing stat considering Everton played with 11 men for almost the entire first half.

Mykolenko was strong in the ground duel and did notch 11 defensive contributions as the Toffees were pinned in, but he also gave away a foul and lost all three of the aerials he contested.

Moyes is not inundated with options in his defence, but there is certainly scope to replace Mykolenko.

James Garner played at left-back when the Ukrainian was injured last season and excelled there, able to drop into midfield in an inverted role.

Merlin Rohl, who has appeared regularly at right-back this season, can likely do a similar job on the left.

And of course, there is Ainsley Maitland-Niles, who started his Everton career superbly but has not even appeared off the bench in the league since defeat to Chelsea.

Moyes is stubborn, but he must surpass some of his own barriers if Everton are to make history this season.

Manchester City will look to climb the Champions League table and restart their season by beating visitors Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday.

The Citizens are seventh with nine points in the league phase and right now occupy one of eight automatic spots for the round of 16, whereas their Italian opponents are 27th with just three points after four gamedays.

City's woes in the Premier League continued on Saturday afternoon, when they were held to a 1-1 stalemate by Fulham, who left their hosts third in the Premier League table.

Enzo Maresca's side have now lost three and drawn one of their past four top-flight outings, while they have won four and lost four of their nine most recent matches.

One of those defeats was a 4-2 loss against Paris Saint-Germain on October 24 in their fourth Champions League clash of the season.

The hosts' defensive frailties were routinely exposed by PSG, and it should concern fans the club have conceded at least two goals in seven of their last 11 fixtures, a period in which they kept just one clean sheet.

Maresca's side have still largely succeeded at home considering they have triumphed in seven of their 10 contests at the Etihad this term, suffering two defeats in that time.

City have conceded 14 goals in their past seven clashes at the stadium, while they managed to find the back of the net on 18 occasions.

Kevin De Bruyne will return to the Etihad once again as a Napoli player, though his side have been defeated in each of their last three meetings with their English hosts.

The visitors appointed Massimiliano Allegri as the successor to Antonio Conte, who won Serie A in 2024-25, the Supercoppa Italiana in 2025-26 and guided the club to second place in May, but the current manager's spell in the dugout has been disastrous.

The visitors have won six of their 16 fixtures this campaign, and they head to the Etihad having been beaten in two of their past four games, emerging as victors once.

Gli Azzurri are eighth in the Serie A table with 18 points following their 1-0 win against Torino on Saturday, and their situation in Europe is also concerning given they have lost to Arsenal, Villarreal and Porto.

They have conceded 11 times so far in the Champions League, and though they have netted six goals, they scored just six goals in their past seven away contests in all competitions.

Napoli were beaten in five of those seven matches on the road, with their only victory a 4-1 win against Monza on October 28.

Donyell Malen would cost £60million if Aston Villa wanted to sign him back from Roma in the coming transfer windows.

That is the opinion of former senior Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The forward left the Villans in January, joining the Italian giants initially on loan before signing permanently in a deal worth a total fee of around £21.5m.

Malen struggled for minutes at Villa, with Unai Emery seemingly unwilling to ever hand him a sustained role in the starting XI during his year at the club.

But in Italy, the Netherlands international has come alive, scoring a staggering 31 goals and providing six assists in just 35 games since arriving.

Malen has hit yet another level this season, scoring or assisting in his last eight games for Roma and netting four against Parma on Saturday.

Il poker di Malen 4️⃣🔥 #ParmaRoma #SerieAEnilive #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/058yCcNrIf.

Villa were held to a 0-0 draw at home to Sunderland on Saturday, marking a fifth consecutive game without victory for Emery's men.

They have failed to score in three of those games, and produced only one major chance against the Black Cats.

Goal-scoring has become quite an problem for Villa, and they may well only have themselves to blame.

"Isn't it funny. The boy they sold to Roma, he can't stop scoring goals," King told Football Insider. "He has scored 12 in the last 11 league games. He got four at the weekend!

According to recent reports, "They took the £2m loan in January, and they bought him in May. He's now a full Roma player. So, if Aston Villa wanted to buy him back, he'd cost £60m.

Recent findings suggest that "Seems like a funny bit of business to me. For a 27-year-old, okay, he might not have been hitting the buttons at Aston Villa, but if they'd have kept [Ollie] Watkins in him, I don't think they'd have goal-scoring problems.

According to recent reports, "They let Watkins go, and this is a 20-goal-a-season man. They brought in [Tammy] Abraham, who struggled. [Nicolas] Jackson's doing okay, but he needs support.".

While the decision to sell Malen has aged woefully, he likely never would have had the same opportunities if he had stayed at Villa.

Of his 46 starts, the 27-year-old started just 14 games and, for whatever reason, clearly was not a player Emery ever fully trusted.

"It was a good deal for us and for him, as he wanted to play as a striker, and we're getting along well with Watkins," the Spaniard said in April.

"I would have liked to keep him, but he wanted to play more and asked me several times. He got this opportunity, and I'm happy for him. He's an excellent player, and I think he can have a great career in Rome.".

A 3-1 loss at Minnesota United on Decision Day meant the Quakes finished fourth in the MLS table out West, while Houston was a point behind them in fifth after a 1-0 home defeat to St Louis City.

After narrowly missing the post-season a year ago, San Jose got the job done this time around, earning 52 points, 11 more than they had in 2025.

Bruce Arena guided them to a 14-win regular season in 2026, the most for this club since 2013, when they also won 14 times.

Heading into the post-season, San Jose are on a six-match MLS unbeaten run at home, winning their last match at PayPal Park 2-1 versus Real Salt Lake on Halloween.

This year they have found the back of the net in all but two MLS affairs at home, while scoring multiple goals on nine occasions.

On Tuesday they can claim their first playoff victory since 2012 and earn their first post-season triumph at home since 2004 (2-0 over the Kansas City Wizards).

The Quakes are unbeaten in their last four MLS games against Houston, blanking them 1-0 at PayPal Park earlier this season.

After failing to make the playoffs for the first time in his tenure last year, Ben Olsen and the Dynamo bounced back with a much more consistent 2026 campaign.

During this regular season, Houston collected 51 points, 14 more than a year ago, while finishing seven places higher in the Western Conference table.

Their 43 goals scored during the regular season were the fewest among the MLS sides that made the playoffs, though they gave up the third fewest in the West (43) as well.

A win in game one would mark the first for this club away from home in the post-season since 2017, when they defeated the Timbers 2-1 in Portland.

John Souttar is struggling to attract suitors as he prepares to leave Rangers permanently in the January transfer window.

The 30-year-old has been cast out under Derek McInnes and has not featured since the manager's arrival during the summer, despite remaining under contract at Ibrox.

He was widely expected to leave during the summer transfer window, but failed to agree terms, and there are now doubts about whether a January move will be forthcoming.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Souttar will find it difficult to land a latest club as concerns about his fitness have now emerged.

Having not played for Rangers this season, the centre-back last started a competitive game of football in May, when he captained Danny Rohl's side to victory against Falkirk.

However, the lack of top-level interest in Souttar during the summer raised early red flags, and there is a growing chance he may have to see out the saeson on the sidelines at Ibrox.

Football Insider revealed back in September that Souttar has no chance of returning to the Rangers side under McInnes and has been told to find a new club in January.

Despite failing to agree a move to any of his suitors during the summer window, there was a growing expectation that he would be more open to opportunities in January.

However, after months on the sidelines, any lingering interest in Souttar has faded and it is becoming increasingly difficult for him to find a destination away from Ibrox.

"I watched John Souttar years ago and I've never been convinced by him," Brown told Football Insider.

"He always looks big, heavy and clumsy, so it wasn't a surprise to me when Derek McInnes decided he wouldn't be part of his aims at Rangers.

According to recent reports, "The problem is, which clubs are going to want him? There aren't any top clubs who are going to be interested, to be honest I'd be surprised if Championship clubs wanted him.

"So he was always going to have to think outside the box a little bit to find a latest club, but he's still struggling to attract interest, and the longer it goes on for, the less likely it becomes.

Recent findings suggest that "Mid-way through the season, you want to sign players who are ready to step in and make a difference. That won't be the case after he's spent months on the sidelines.

Industry observers note that "So it's going to be a real problem for him, where does he end up? Maybe he could stay at Rangers for the rest of the season, but then it's an entire season wasted.".

As previously mentioned, Souttar is going to have to think outside the box when it comes to deciding his next club, with a shortage of interest from top sides in Europe.

Football Insider revealed in September that Greek outfit Aris Thessaloniki were working on a deal to sign Souttar and had hoped to get an agreement over the line.

However, that deal eventually fell through at the end of the Greek window and left Souttar stranded at Rangers, at least until the mid-season window opens.

There are now doubts, though, about whether Aris could return with a latest offer after he has spent months on the sidelines, and he may be forced to look elsewhere yet again.

Like Bayern, however, PSG will almost certainly meet a categorical refusal from Roma, at least in January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Matthijs de Ligt cannot remain a first-choice option for Manchester United when he continues to make glaring errors.

The 27-year-old has faced questions about his long-term furture at Old Trafford as a result of his injury problems, but was thrust into Mauricio Pochettino's first starting XI.

While the manager has faced some backlash and confusion over what proved to be a misguided decisions, there are now calls for the centre-back to be left out again.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that De Ligt does not possess any attributes that would make him a regular starter for Pochettino's side.

A lack of top-class defenders has left the manager in a difficult position, but after it has become clear that he is not up to scratch, the Netherlands international must be left out.

Plans can then be put in place to replace De Ligt, whether it happens in January or next summer, as the Red Devils strategy an overhaul of their back line in the transfer window.

Former Tottenham scout Bryan King told Football Insider on 23 November that Pochettino will have to overhaul the XI that started against Liverpool last time out.

Major changes will have to take place under the new manager, who has been given an illustration of why Michael Carrick struggled to get results out of this side.

De Ligt is one of a few players who have come under fire since the defeat, but amid longer-term questions about his future in the side, he could be cast out of Man United.

"I couldn't believe Pochettino threw De Ligt straight back into the starting XI," Brown told Football Insider.

"I don't know whether he was poorly advised or just wanted to try something different, but he was never going to be ready to step straight in and make a real difference.

"It was partly his mistake that led to Yoro getting sent off, and he looked miles off the standard you would expect from a Man United defender.

"He cannot be a regular in this side, it's as simple as that, there were doubts about him before he got injured and he's only just coming back from months on the sidelines.

It has been revealed that "It's a difficult situation for Pochettino, because where does he turn? It's clear something has got to change, because they've been shocking defensively.

"De Ligt cannot continue in that back line, there's doubts about Martinez, Yoro has made too many mistakes, Heaven is still only young, the only one I'd trust is Harry Maguire.

"It's a position that's going to need serious investment, because there are four or five players who need replacing, and I think De Ligt has to be one of the first cast out.".

Man United have got the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues this season, and have been left scrambling to make changes and improve their back line.

Given the limited options available to Pochettino, there have been calls for a number of regular starters to be axed, as it has become clear that something has got to change.

Football Insider reported on 23 November that Lisandro Martinez should be dropped from Pochettino's starting XI after what was a dismal showing against Liverpool.

This has been a terrible season overall for the Argentina centre-back, with error-ridden performances leading to questions about his long-term future at the club.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, has also cast doubts over his position in the XI after picking up a red card at Anfield, leaving Pochettino with very few reliable options to call upon.

Industry News: Feyenoord vs Porto - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Feyenoord will be desperate to end a six-match winless run when they welcome Porto to De Kuip for Tuesday's Champions League league-phase encounter.
  • Both sides have collected just three points from their opening four European fixtures, leaving the Portuguese visitors 26th in the 36-team table and their Dutch hosts languishing in 32nd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 22 Nov 2026 18:17, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:45.

Feyenoord will be desperate to end a six-match winless run when they welcome Porto to De Kuip for Tuesday's Champions League league-phase encounter.

Both sides have collected just three points from their opening four European fixtures, leaving the Portuguese visitors 26th in the 36-team table and their Dutch hosts languishing in 32nd.

Feyenoord head into Tuesday's encounter after suffering three consecutive defeats, the latest of which came at De Kuip on Saturday when they were beaten 3-2 by Excelsior, who secured their first league victory at the ground in 46 years.

The hosts made a bright start by taking the lead through Givairo Read barely two minutes into the contest, but three goals in succession left Jan Plug's own goal little more than a consolation as De Stadionclub slipped to fifth in the Eredivisie table.

More concerning for Giovanni van Bronckhorst is his side's defensive record, having conceded at least three goals in each of their last three outings across all competitions, with Saturday's setback following a 5-3 defeat at Heerenveen and a 3-0 home loss to Inter Milan on matchday four of the Champions League league phase.

That continental defeat was the 10th in Feyenoord's last 13 European matches, while it also extended an unwanted run that has seen them concede the opening goal in each of their last seven Champions League outings, including defeats to Barcelona and Real Betis as well as their victory over Como on matchday two.

With the prospect of another early European exit looming, the Dutch club know that another setback on Tuesday would leave their hopes of reaching the knockout rounds hanging by a thread, having already fallen short in last season's Europa League league phase, where they finished 29th.

However, the hosts face a difficult examination against a Porto side who finally got their Champions League campaign up and running with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Napoli at the Estadio do Dragao on matchday four.

Francesco Farioli's men had suffered defeats to Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV in their opening three league-phase fixtures, but goals from Jan Bednarek, Gabri Veiga, Jakub Kiwior and Samu Omorodion inspired a convincing response against the Italian outfit.

That being said, Porto have won each of their opening 11 league matches this term to establish a five-point gap atop the Primeira Liga table, though the Dragons were made to work harder in Friday's Taca de Portugal encounter with third-tier Paredes, eventually progressing on penalties after a 1-1 draw across 120 minutes.

Back on the continental stage, the Dragons, featuring in the Champions League main stage for the first time in three years, will continue their quest to reach the knockout rounds for the third consecutive appearance, having progressed to the last 16 in their previous two campaigns.

Nevertheless, the visitors have not always enjoyed travelling to the Netherlands, failing to win any of their last four away matches against Dutch opposition (D2, L2), including  both previous visits to Feyenoord, having drawn at De Kuip in the Champions League in 1993 before suffering a 2-0 defeat there in 2019, while both of Porto’s victories in this fixture have come on home soil.

Feyenoord Champions League form:.

Feyenoord form (all competitions):.

Feyenoord are monitoring the fitness of Anis Hadj Moussa, who returned from international duty with an ankle injury and missed Saturday's defeat to Excelsior.

Tsuyoshi Watanabe is also doubtful after being withdrawn at half time against Excelsior, with Van Bronckhorst indicating that the defender was struggling with a foot problem, while Jakub Moder and Bart Nieuwkoop remain sidelined with injuries.

Industry observers note that thomas Beelen (leg), Jordan Bos (ACL) and Jerry St. Juste (shin) are expected to remain unavailable, leaving the hosts with limited defensive options.

Former Arsenal winger Reiss Nelson made his first start for Feyenoord at the weekend, although Luciano Valente could be preferred on the left flank of attack against Porto.

As for the visitors, long-term absentee Vasco Sousa remains sidelined with a leg injury, while William Gomes has recovered from an ankle injury and returned to full training, although his involvement on Tuesday remains uncertain.

Former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling is also dealing with a right knee problem and is ineligible to feature, having not been included in Porto's Champions League league-phase squad.

Midfielder In-beom Hwang will face his former club after joining Porto from Feyenoord over the summer, while on-loan striker Santiago Gimenez returns to the Netherlands after representing the Dutch side between 2022 and 2025.

Feyenoord possible starting lineup:.

Ernst; Read, Kraaijeveld, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Valente, Hadj Moussa; Ferri.

Porto possible starting lineup:.

Diogo Costa; Alberto Costa, Bednarek, Kiwior, Zaidu; Veiga, Rosario, Froholdt; Pepe, Sainz, Andre Silva.

Feyenoord's six-match winless run and continued defensive problems make it difficult to back the hosts, particularly against a Porto side who highlighted what they are capable of with their emphatic victory over Napoli.

The Portuguese visitors have also enjoyed the better of this fixture historically, and we expect them to take advantage of the host’s current struggles to secure their first away victory at De Kuip.
